item.title: College Football Playoff Projections Roundup for the Kentucky Wildcats
item.description: Two weeks ago, I admitted I had a gut feeling. Every week when I sat down to figure out where this Kentucky Football team was headed, the answer in my head was PLAYOFFS. Said loudly, in my best Jim Mora voice. Back then, it felt a little crazy. After the LSU win, only three of ESPN’s 11 experts had Kentucky in their playoff field, and Heather Dinich had the Cats as the 12th team in. Now? Kentucky is getting a lot more playoff love following Saturday’s 34-17 victory over Vanderbilt, putting the Wildcats in first place in the SEC standings. It wasn’t pretty early. Vandy jumped out to a 10-0 lead in the second quarter, and for a while, it looked like the Cats might get caught in the same trap that took down a bunch of ranked teams the past two Saturdays. Then, Kentucky outscored the Commodores 34-7 the rest of the way while looking much more like a team capable of earning a playoff spot. Kenny Minchey went 19/26 for 203 yards and a touchdown. Freshman Kenny Darby caught five passes for 71 yards, including a 44-yarder that set up Kentucky’s first touchdown of the second half. Backup quarterback Brennen Ward got the first carry of his career and turned it into a 10-yard touchdown run. And the defense held Vanderbilt to 15 rushing yards on 17 carries. Fifteen. Will Stein said afterward that his team is hungry and not satisfied, and that the goal is a November to remember. Kentucky is 7-1 (5-1 SEC) and sits alone in first place in the SEC, a half game ahead of Georgia. The Coaches Poll moved the Cats up four spots to No. 8 in the country. Kentucky is a top-10 team. Read that one more time. The new AP Poll had Kentucky up from No. 12 to No. 9. A few nuggets from another historic week: Stein is the first Kentucky coach to start 7-1 in his first season since E.R. Sweetland in 1909. That’s 117 years. Kentucky has won five straight SEC games for the first time since 1977. The Cats have won six straight since the Week 2 loss to Alabama. Kentucky has clinched a winning SEC record for just the third time since 1977. Where Kentucky stands in the College Football Playoff Projections After the LSU win, Kentucky was a fun maybe. After Oklahoma, a popular pick. After Vanderbilt, Kentucky is a unanimous one. Every major national projection I could find has the Wildcats in the 12-team field, and the seeds now range from No. 6 to No. 9. CBS Sports (Brad Crawford): No. 6 seed, hosting No. 11 Notre Dame (up from No. 10 last week) Sports Illustrated (Bryan Fischer): No. 6 seed, hosting No. 11 Florida On3 (Andy Staples): No. 7 seed, hosting No. 10 Florida, with the winner facing No. 2 Ohio State in the Rose Bowl (up from No. 9) Sporting News (Bill Bender): No. 8 seed, hosting No. 9 BYU ESPN (Heather Dinich): No. 9 And the ESPN expert panel, which had just three of 11 voters putting Kentucky in after LSU: Adam Rittenberg: No. 6 Bill Connelly: No. 7 David Hale: No. 7 Alex Scarborough: No. 7 Mark Schlabach: No. 7 Dave Wilson: No. 7 Eli Lederman: No. 8 Jake Trotter: No. 8 Paol
item.content:encoded: Two weeks ago, I admitted I had a gut feeling. Every week when I sat down to figure out where this Kentucky Football team was headed, the answer in my head was PLAYOFFS. Said loudly, in my best Jim Mora voice. Back then, it felt a little crazy. After the LSU win, only three of ESPN’s 11 experts had Kentucky in their playoff field, and Heather Dinich had the Cats as the 12th team in. Now? Kentucky is getting a lot more playoff love following Saturday’s 34-17 victory over Vanderbilt, putting the Wildcats in first place in the SEC standings. It wasn’t pretty early. Vandy jumped out to a 10-0 lead in the second quarter, and for a while, it looked like the Cats might get caught in the same trap that took down a bunch of ranked teams the past two Saturdays. Then, Kentucky outscored the Commodores 34-7 the rest of the way while looking much more like a team capable of earning a playoff spot. Kenny Minchey went 19/26 for 203 yards and a touchdown. Freshman Kenny Darby caught five passes for 71 yards, including a 44-yarder that set up Kentucky’s first touchdown of the second half. Backup quarterback Brennen Ward got the first carry of his career and turned it into a 10-yard touchdown run. And the defense held Vanderbilt to 15 rushing yards on 17 carries. Fifteen. Will Stein said afterward that his team is hungry and not satisfied, and that the goal is a November to remember. Kentucky is 7-1 (5-1 SEC) and sits alone in first place in the SEC, a half game ahead of Georgia. The Coaches Poll moved the Cats up four spots to No. 8 in the country. Kentucky is a top-10 team. Read that one more time. The new AP Poll had Kentucky up from No. 12 to No. 9. A few nuggets from another historic week: Stein is the first Kentucky coach to start 7-1 in his first season since E.R. Sweetland in 1909. That’s 117 years. Kentucky has won five straight SEC games for the first time since 1977. The Cats have won six straight since the Week 2 loss to Alabama. Kentucky has clinched a winning SEC record for just the third time since 1977. Where Kentucky stands in the College Football Playoff Projections After the LSU win, Kentucky was a fun maybe. After Oklahoma, a popular pick. After Vanderbilt, Kentucky is a unanimous one. Every major national projection I could find has the Wildcats in the 12-team field, and the seeds now range from No. 6 to No. 9. CBS Sports (Brad Crawford): No. 6 seed, hosting No. 11 Notre Dame (up from No. 10 last week) Sports Illustrated (Bryan Fischer): No. 6 seed, hosting No. 11 Florida On3 (Andy Staples): No. 7 seed, hosting No. 10 Florida, with the winner facing No. 2 Ohio State in the Rose Bowl (up from No. 9) Sporting News (Bill Bender): No. 8 seed, hosting No. 9 BYU ESPN (Heather Dinich): No. 9 And the ESPN expert panel, which had just three of 11 voters putting Kentucky in after LSU: Adam Rittenberg: No. 6 Bill Connelly: No. 7 David Hale: No. 7 Alex Scarborough: No. 7 Mark Schlabach: No. 7 Dave Wilson: No. 7 Eli Lederman: No. 8 Jake Trotter: No. 8 Paolo Uggetti: No. 8 Andrea Adelson: No. 9 Kyle Bonagura: No. 9 Max Olson: No. 9 Twelve for twelve. Notice something else. Seeds 5 through 8 host first-round games. Most of these projections now have Kentucky hosting a playoff game at Kroger Field in December. Two weeks ago we were talking about a trip to Bloomington. Now, we’re talking about Notre Dame, Florida, or BYU coming to Lexington. Crawford went further than anyone. He said Stein should be the frontrunner for national coach of the year after the wins over LSU and at Oklahoma. On3’s Ari Wasserman, who has Kentucky No. 8 in his top 10, admitted the Alabama blowout made everyone think this build would take a while. On the playoff question, he wrote that it’s “easier to argue for it than against it.” The bye week and the first CFP rankings Kentucky is off this Saturday, and the timing could not be better. The Cats get a week to get healthy before the stretch run. It also means Kentucky’s resume is locked in before the College Football Playoff selection committee releases its first rankings on Tuesday, Nov. 3. Dinich pointed this out herself: with the bye, Kentucky’s resume is complete before that first ranking comes out. So when the committee reveals its top 25, Kentucky will be in it. The only question is where. Dinich explained why that number matters so much. Teams have historically been better off losing early than late, and that first ranking will show how much margin for error Kentucky has in November. And I’ll say what I’ve been saying for weeks. My pick: PLAYOFFS. And I’m not whispering it anymore. What’s next This is where it gets real. Kentucky’s true place in the playoff picture gets decided in November, with three straight games against ranked teams before the Governor’s Cup. Oct. 31: Bye Nov. 3: First College Football Playoff rankings Nov. 7: at Tennessee Nov. 14: Florida Nov. 21: at Missouri Nov. 28: Louisville Two weeks ago I asked if this was likely. The answer was no, but it was possible. Today, with Kentucky alone in first place in the SEC and in every projection in the country, the answer has changed. It’s not just possible anymore. It’s real. Saying this, it’s on the Kentucky players and coaches to keep this dream going. What they’ve done thus far has been unbelievable and brought tremendous joy to the BBN. But to make the playoff, they’ll have to continue improving every single day, as all four of their remaining opponents can beat the Cats if they don’t come ready to play. Or, as Will Stein says, “One play at a time. One-play focus.”

item.title: Detroit Lions vs. Minnesota Vikings Point Spread Revealed
item.description: The Detroit Lions are coming off a thrilling 20-17 victory over the Green Bay Packers, and oddsmakers have already released the opening point spread for their next NFC North showdown. Despite the Minnesota Vikings entering the matchup undefeated, Detroit has opened as a 3-point favorite for Sunday’s Week 8 contest at Ford Field. According to FanDuel Sportsbook , the Lions are favored by a field goal against Minnesota, which improved to 6-0 following Sunday’s 16-10 victory over the Indianapolis Colts. Detroit, meanwhile, improved to 4-2 after Jake Bates connected on a game-winning field goal against Green Bay. Oct 25, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Detroit Lions head coach Dan Campbell reacts to a call during the second quarter against the Green Bay Packers at Ford Field. Mandatory Credit: Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Detroit Lions vs. Minnesota Vikings Betting Odds Here are the opening betting lines for the November 1 matchup, according to FanDuel Sportsbook on Sunday evening, October 25. Betting market Minnesota Vikings Detroit Lions Point spread +3 (-106) -3 (-114) Moneyline +138 -164 Over/Under Over 46.5 (-104) Under 46.5 (-118) The 3-point spread indicates that oddsmakers expect a competitive matchup, even with Minnesota entering the game without a loss. Detroit’s -164 moneyline means the Lions are favored to win outright, while the Vikings offer a +138 return for those backing an upset. The total of 46.5 points suggests a game in which both offenses could have opportunities to score, although Minnesota’s defense has been one of the biggest reasons for its undefeated start. As always, these betting lines are subject to change throughout the week. Lions Looking to Build on Packers Victory Detroit enters Week 8 with momentum after surviving a difficult battle against Green Bay, despite a controversial fourth-down decision by head coach Dan Campbell late in the game. The Lions finished with 415 total yards, while Jared Goff threw for 303 yards and two touchdowns in the victory. Jameson Williams was one of Detroit’s biggest offensive weapons, finishing with five receptions for 91 yards and two touchdowns. As we previously reported , the Lions’ schedule features consecutive home games against the Packers and Vikings, giving Detroit an opportunity to make significant progress in the NFC North standings. There is also plenty at stake beyond Sunday’s point spread, particularly with Minnesota sitting atop the division. A Lions victory would hand the Vikings their first loss of 2026 and move Detroit closer to the division lead. Lions Will Have Extra Motivation Against Vikings The Lions have another reason to be motivated heading into Sunday’s matchup, as Minnesota won both meetings between the teams during the 2025 season. Detroit may be favored by three points, but knocking off an undefeated division rival will require another strong performance from Campbell’s squad.

item.title: Big 12 football standings, results after Week 8 of 2026 season
item.description: The Big 12 had a chaotic weekend. It started with Cincinnati outplaying Texas Tech, who won just their second conference game of the season. BYU also fell in one of the wildest games you will ever see, with a blocked field goal to end regulation and multiple penalties by the Cougars that kept UCF alive. For a while, it looked like Utah might join the chaos after narrowly escaping last week with a win over Colorado . However, they fought back in the second half to become the only undefeated team left in the Big 12 and dropped Houston to two conference losses, effectively eliminating their chances of making the Big 12 championship. Here is how the Big 12 standings look after Week 8. Hockenson #87 of the Minnesota Vikings celebrates with Justin Jefferson #18 after scoring a touchdown against the Indianapolis Colts during the fourth quarter of the game at U.S. Bank Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. item.title: Falcons hand 49ers first defeat of NFL season, Vikings remain unbeaten
item.description: Jessie Bates III of the Atlanta Falcons punches the ball out from George Kittle in the Falcons' NFL victory over the San Francisco 49ers (Todd Kirkland) Michael Penix threw for three touchdowns and the Atlanta defense forced four turnovers as the Falcons beat San Francisco 29-20 to deal the 49ers their first defeat of the NFL season on Sunday. San Francisco quarterback Brock Purdy was intercepted twice, George Kittle and Kaelon Black gave up fumbles and a thigh injury to Christian McCaffrey further hindered the 49ers' depleted receiving corps. One week after he was stretchered off after taking a knee to the head, Atlanta's rookie linebacker Kendal Daniels intercepted a Purdy pass intended for Jordan Watkins with 2:34 remaining and recovered Kittle's fumble with less than a minute to go to secure their first home win of the season and improve to 3-4. "It was all complementary football," Penix said. "Offense, defense, special teams, everybody played well today." Penix connected with tight end Nick Muse for a touchdown to keep the Falcons within striking distance in the first half and hit Kyle Pitts for a TD that put Atlanta ahead in the third quarter. He found Drake London with a 21-yard touchdown pass in the fourth. McCaffrey had capped a 10-play, 64-yard opening drive with a one-yard touchdown leap on fourth down to give San Francisco a quick 7-0 lead. But he missed much of the first half with a thigh injury and despite his return in the second half the 49ers couldn't come back. "Any time you have four turnovers like that and you get zero, it's real tough to win," 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said. "Too sloppy to win." While the 49ers fell to 6-1, the Minnesota Vikings remained unbeaten, holding the Indianapolis Colts scoreless in the second half in a 16-10 victory that saw them improve to 6-0. Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray threw a five-yard touchdown pass to T.J. Hockenson early in the fourth quarter and Will Reichard kicked a 52-yard field goal with 1:39 remaining. Minnesota's Harrison Smith picked off Colts quarterback Daniel Jones in the final minute to preserve the win. It was the 40th career interception for the 15-year veteran. The Vikings remained as one of two unbeaten teams. The Kansas City Chiefs were seeking to improve to 6-0 when they took on the Super Bowl champion Seahawks in Seattle. - Steelers win in Paris- Sunday's action kicked off in Paris, where Pittsburgh quarterback Aaron Rodgers threw for 212 yards and a milestone touchdown to lead the Steelers to a 16-10 victory over the New Orleans Saints in the league's first regular-season game in the French capital. Rodgers hit Darnell Washington with a four-yard TD pass to give the Steelers a 10-3 lead late in the second quarter, his 540th regular-season touchdown pass moving him into solo third place on the all-time list ahead of Peyton Manning (539). The Los Angeles Rams snapped a two-game skid in emphatic style, beating the Raiders 35-21 in Las Vegas. Rams quarterback Matthew Staf

While the 49ers fell to 6-1, the Minnesota Vikings remained unbeaten, holding the Indianapolis Colts scoreless in the second half in a 16-10 victory that saw them improve to 6-0. The Los Angeles Rams snapped a two-game skid in emphatic style, beating the Raiders 35-21 in Las Vegas. Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford threw for 195 yards and three touchdowns, all in the first half. He became the franchise leader in scoring passes -- an honor Stafford also holds with the Detroit Lions. "More importantly, happy for our guys," Stafford said. "We've had some tough losses late in games this year, played good enough football to win games and hadn't gotten it done ... proud of our resolve and our ability to get the win." In Houston, Devin Singletary ran 30 yards for a touchdown in overtime to lift the New York Giants to a 27-21 upset win over the Texans. In Detroit, Jake Bates kicked a 22-yard field goal as time expired to give the Lions a 20-17 victory over the Green Bay Packers. Cincinnati quarterback Joe Burrow threw four touchdown passes in the second half as the Bengals rallied to beat the Ravens 35-13 in Baltimore. Cleveland quarterback Deshaun Watson piloted his fifth fourth-quarter game-winning drive of the season, capped by Andre Szmyt's 32-yard field goal as time expired in the Browns' 27-24 victory over the Tennessee Titans in Nashville. And the Miami Dolphins earned their first win of the season, beating the New York Jets 28-25 in New Jersey. bb/amz

item.title: Kansas City Chiefs at Seattle Seahawks, Week 7 ‘SNF’ open thread
item.description: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - OCTOBER 25: Patrick Mahomes #15 of the Kansas City Chiefs warms up against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field on October 25, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Caleb Bowlin/Getty Images) | Getty Images Well, Rumblers, we’ve a bit of a rare one on deck this evening. Strange enough, the Kansas City Chiefs do actually play primetime games away from Arrowhead Stadium, and tonight they’re in the Northwest to face the Seattle Seahawks. Buffalo Bills fans need zero reminders about rooting interests here: Tonight you’re part of the 12th Man in an attempt to hand the Chiefs their first loss of the season. Back in January, this is a game that wouldn’t have held the same amount of intrigue, and for sure wouldn’t have seemed favorable to Kansas City. Yet here we are, with the Chiefs undefeated at 5-0, and the Seahawks a middling 3-3. With the Bills on their bye, all the fan base can do this weekend is cheer on the enemy of their enemy. That makes Seattle your favorite team this evening (please don’t wear ugly uniforms, Seahawks). However, the reverse jinx is also an option: It sure would be great for the Bills if their bye started with a loss for the New England Patriots, and ended (essentially, because who cares about that NFC East matchup for Monday Night Football ?) with the Chiefs losing in primetime. Is everything coming up Milhouse?! With that, here’s your open thread for Week 7 of Sunday Night Football . As always, be kind to one another — and in all things… Go Bills!

item.title: ‘There’s no way’: Tom Brady does not hold back on referees on Fox broadcast
item.description: Oct 27, 2024; Seattle, Washington, USA; FOX commentator Tom Brady stands on the sideline before a game between the Seattle Seahawks and Buffalo Bills at Lumen Field. Mandatory Credit: Joe Nicholson-Imagn Images The Detroit Lions beat the Green Bay Packers 20-17 on Sunday thanks to a Jake Bates field goal on the final play. But the officials played a big role in the outcome, too, and analyst Tom Brady wasn’t happy about it. Calling the game for Fox, Brady repeatedly took issue with the penalties, including a roughing the passer call on the Packers that helped set up Detroit’s game-winning drive. Questionable Calls The Lions improved to 4-2 with the win, while the Packers fell to 4-3. But several of the game’s biggest moments came down to flags. The Packers were hit with two questionable roughing the passer calls, including one on Karl Brooks during the Lions’ final drive as Detroit then went 71 yards in 10 plays to set up the winning kick. The Lions weren’t spared, either. Before that drive, linebacker Derrick Barnes was flagged for a questionable unnecessary roughness penalty after a hit on Packers running back MarShawn Lloyd that gave Green Bay an automatic first down on a drive where they ultimately tied the game at 17. ‘That’s Allowed 99 Out Of 100’ Brady made it pretty clear that he didn’t agree with the call on Barnes’ hit. After hearing that a flag was on the way, he responded, “There’s no way,” and when the penalty was announced, he added, “Come on, man.” “Oh, he’s just turning his right shoulder away from it. That’s allowed 99 out of 100,” Brady said, via Awful Announcing . Tom Brady has had it with the NFL officiating. https://t.co/aJlsmpDfza — Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) October 25, 2026 “Yeah, it’s a bang-bang play. I know in super slow-mo every little minute frame looks like a lot, but when you’re on the field, you’ve got to pursue that ball,” Brady continued. “If he catches it, he needs force to knock him on the ground. He needs force to knock that ball off him as a pass defense. He can’t go in there and put his hand on him.” ‘Definitely Not Roughing The Passer’ Later in the fourth quarter, Brooks was flagged for roughing the passer for a hit against Jared Goff with 2:40 left, and Brady was even more frustrated. “No, my goodness, what is that? There’s no way,” Brady said, via Awful Announcing . “That’s definitely not roughing the passer. I mean, you just— you’re just ripping through the line of scrimmage to try to get the quarterback on the ground. Look, I love Goff standing there in the pocket, but you just can’t keep tacking on 15 yards.” Fox rules analyst Dean Blandino agreed with Brady. Tom Brady has had it with the NFL officiating. https://t.co/aJlsmpDfza — Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) October 25, 2026 “It wasn’t late. They might have said head-neck area, but this is not head-neck area. His head is up. That’s teach-tape tackle. That’s not roughing the passer,” Blandino said. Play-by-play announcer Kevin Burkhardt

item.title: 5 takeaways from Lions’ victory against Packers
item.description: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - OCTOBER 25: Penei Sewell #58 of the Detroit Lions leads a huddle prior to a game against the Green Bay Packers at Ford Field on October 25, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images Coming off a bye week, the Detroit Lions got extra time to prepare for the Green Bay Packers in their first NFC North battle of 2026. This game was much closer than it should’ve been, as Detroit dominated and its own mistakes gave Green Bay life. It came down to a game-winning kick by kicker Jake Bates, with Detroit winning 20-17. Here are my five takeaways from the Lions’ thrilling win against the Packers. When the offense was consistent, it was dominant Despite scoring only 20 points, the Lions offense was great when it clicked. They had an opening-drive touchdown for the first time this season, moving the ball downfield with ease as they scored in under four minutes on six plays to take the lead. Quarterback Jared Goff was wheeling and dealing, going 22-for-32 for 303 yards and two touchdowns. Jameson Williams' 2nd TD of the game and the Lions take the lead back! GBvsDET on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/crTR8JKgaZ — NFL (@NFL) October 25, 2026 Wide receiver Jameson Williams found the end zone for Detroit, catching five for 91 yards and two touchdowns. Lions’ leading receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown had his biggest game of the season, getting nine catches for 153 yards. The passing attack was lethal and picked apart the Packers’ secondary, which relies on its safeties to bail it out. Play action worked with ease, given Green Bay’s lack of depth at linebacker. Running back Jahmyr Gibbs had highs and lows, finishing with 29 carries for 116 yards and five catches for 27 yards. His second-quarter fumble was costly, as it killed Detroit’s chance to at least take a six-point lead at the half after they got the ball back. In the end, Gibbs clutched up and helped set Bates up for the game-winning kick. The return of Brian Branch and Cade Mays was felt Two big pieces returned for the Lions on Sunday: safety Brian Branch and center Cade Mays. Mays started at center, and the offensive line struck consistently in the passing game as play-action gave Goff time to let it rip. The running game showed flashes of success. Mays did make a mistake, though, and bumped into Gibbs on the first fumble of the game. Branch wasn’t on the field as often as Mays, as his Achilles injury will take time to adjust to playing again. Despite getting limited snaps, Branch had an impact with four tackles and a huge interception in the fourth quarter. The secondary did improve with Branch back, and Mays gave the offensive line a nice boost. These two players had a big impact in the win, and the team feels like it has a better identity on offense and defense. Branch back y'all pic.twitter.com/vjACYfESmQ — Detroit Lions (@Lions) October 25, 2026 Defense crumbles on crucial downs Detroit’s defense has improved in its past two games,
item.content:encoded: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - OCTOBER 25: Penei Sewell #58 of the Detroit Lions leads a huddle prior to a game against the Green Bay Packers at Ford Field on October 25, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images Coming off a bye week, the Detroit Lions got extra time to prepare for the Green Bay Packers in their first NFC North battle of 2026. This game was much closer than it should’ve been, as Detroit dominated and its own mistakes gave Green Bay life. It came down to a game-winning kick by kicker Jake Bates, with Detroit winning 20-17. Here are my five takeaways from the Lions’ thrilling win against the Packers. When the offense was consistent, it was dominant Despite scoring only 20 points, the Lions offense was great when it clicked. They had an opening-drive touchdown for the first time this season, moving the ball downfield with ease as they scored in under four minutes on six plays to take the lead. Quarterback Jared Goff was wheeling and dealing, going 22-for-32 for 303 yards and two touchdowns. Jameson Williams' 2nd TD of the game and the Lions take the lead back! GBvsDET on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/crTR8JKgaZ — NFL (@NFL) October 25, 2026 Wide receiver Jameson Williams found the end zone for Detroit, catching five for 91 yards and two touchdowns. Lions’ leading receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown had his biggest game of the season, getting nine catches for 153 yards. The passing attack was lethal and picked apart the Packers’ secondary, which relies on its safeties to bail it out. Play action worked with ease, given Green Bay’s lack of depth at linebacker. Running back Jahmyr Gibbs had highs and lows, finishing with 29 carries for 116 yards and five catches for 27 yards. His second-quarter fumble was costly, as it killed Detroit’s chance to at least take a six-point lead at the half after they got the ball back. In the end, Gibbs clutched up and helped set Bates up for the game-winning kick. The return of Brian Branch and Cade Mays was felt Two big pieces returned for the Lions on Sunday: safety Brian Branch and center Cade Mays. Mays started at center, and the offensive line struck consistently in the passing game as play-action gave Goff time to let it rip. The running game showed flashes of success. Mays did make a mistake, though, and bumped into Gibbs on the first fumble of the game. Branch wasn’t on the field as often as Mays, as his Achilles injury will take time to adjust to playing again. Despite getting limited snaps, Branch had an impact with four tackles and a huge interception in the fourth quarter. The secondary did improve with Branch back, and Mays gave the offensive line a nice boost. These two players had a big impact in the win, and the team feels like it has a better identity on offense and defense. Branch back y'all pic.twitter.com/vjACYfESmQ — Detroit Lions (@Lions) October 25, 2026 Defense crumbles on crucial downs Detroit’s defense has improved in its past two games, but its biggest problem this week was stopping the Packers on crucial downs. Green Bay was three-for-four on fourth-down attempts, getting 77 yards on those successful plays. On third-down, gotta-have-it stops, the Lions let the Packers go five-for-15. While that isn’t a high success rate, Green Bay converted on those downs and turned it into points almost every time. Opening drive – Converted fourth down, set up a field goal that was missed Second drive – Converted two third downs and one fourth down; result was a touchdown Third drive – Three-and-out Fourth drive – Converted one third and one fourth down; was stopped on downs on the lone failed fourth-down attempt Fifth drive – One rushing play before halftime Sixth drive – Scored touchdown pass on third down pass Seventh drive – Three-and-out Eighth drive – Interception on third down Ninth drive – Converted one third down, made field goal 10th drive – Missed field goal on four-play drive Detroit got bailed out by Packers kicker Trey Smack, who missed two field goals. If he’d made the first field goal, Green Bay might have kicked it on that fourth drive instead of going for it. Green Bay punted only twice all game, and if Detroit makes more stops, those punt numbers could rise. Penalties got cleaned up One issue Detroit has had this season is the number of penalties they’ve gotten in every game. From false starts to holding on either side of the ball, Detroit has been beating itself up in some games this season. On Sunday, Detroit got called for five penalties, a slight improvement from their average of seven per game, according to TeamRankings.com. Two were on special teams, one was a questionable penalty on linebacker Derrick Barnes, and the other two were false starts by the offensive line. The two offensive penalties didn’t hurt the team or stall the drive, which was good to see compared to earlier this year. Unfortunately, when they fix one problem, another one appears. Turnovers were costly While Detroit wasn’t beating themselves with penalties, they beat themselves up with fumbles. While the Gibbs fumble was friendly fire, it still made the game closer than it was. If Gibbs hadn’t fumbled it there, Detroit could have gone up by six to 10 at halftime. Detroit was moving the ball down the field with ease, and it killed the momentum. The second turnover was another awkward play by Mays and Goff; Mays hiked it, and I don’t know what happened. I don’t know if Goff didn’t grasp the ball or Mays snapped it too early, but it was kicked forward, and Green Bay got the ball to start both halves pretty much. While the first fumble didn’t give Green Bay points, the Packers capitalized on the second fumble and scored. Those two fumbles were big swings, and they almost turned this victory into a defeat. Detroit has to clean up the fumbles, and Goff threw multiple risky passes that should have been picked off; one was eliminated due to defensive pass interference on Green Bay. It was scary after the offense started strong, but if they can play clean football and avoid penalties and turnovers, this offense can stay one of the best in the NFL.

item.title: Giants’ Cam Skattebo calls out NFL double standard after ridiculous penalty during Texans game
item.description: Troy Taormina-Imagn Images Giants’ Cam Skattebo calls out NFL double standard after ridiculous penalty during Texans game appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New York Giants are 4-2-1 on the season after defeating the Houston Texans 27-21 on Sunday. It was a great performance for running back Cam Skattebo , as he played a key part in helping his team get the win. However, after the game, Skattebo had some choice words for the NFL after being penalized for lowering his helmet. The 24-year-old was given a 15-yard unnecessary roughness penalty during the contest after delivering a hard hit on Texans safety M.J. Stewart. After the game, Skattebo claimed that he has no intention of changing his playing style and called out the NFL a bit for consistently hyping him up for how he plays football, but then turning around and penalizing him for playing hard. “The NFL loves to post me when I do stuff like that,” Skattebo said. “But then also wants to take stuff from me. If I’m going to continue to get flagged for it, or fined for it, I guess I’m going to play for free.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) While the second-year pro did lower his shoulder and deliver a hard hit, the contact looked rather similar to what you’d see in old Mike Alstott highlights. Skattebo just ran through Stewart on the play, and it would have been a clean play back in the day. #Giants RB Cam Skattebo just absolutely obliterated #Texans S M.J. Stewart—but was called for unnecessary roughness for lowering his helmet. This is not the NFL you grew up watching. pic.twitter.com/6jt8xE4qXP — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) October 25, 2026 Truth be told, the NFL has seemingly enjoyed sharing Cam Skattebo hits . Whether it’s commercials or highlights, the former Arizona State Sun Devils star has built a reputation for being a hard-hitting running back. After essentially being benched in the previous game, Skattebo turned things around against the Texans. He finished the day with 124 rushing yards and a touchdown on 17 attempts. Related: Giants’ Cam Skattebo thankful for bye week after late injury scare on heroic OT run Related: Giants’ J.J. McCarthy, Cam Skattebo walk into Houston and torch Texans. You read that right

item.title: George Russell admits US Grand Prix pace was ‘rubbish’ as Antonelli closes in on F1 title
item.description: George Russell acknowledged his pace was “rubbish” in Austin on Sunday after he just about stretched the F1 title race to Mexico City next week. Russell, starting in sixth, was given a five-second time penalty early on at the US Grand Prix for a clash with Oscar Piastri and then struggled for speed, coming home in only eighth place. Mercedes teammate Kimi Antonelli , meanwhile, claimed his ninth win of the season and now only needs to finish ninth next week in Mexico to seal his first world championship. It was another tough Sunday pill for Russell to swallow and the Briton, who was the heavy title favourite ahead of the season, admitted he “does not have the answers” to his issues right now. “The pace was rubbish today – that's the long and short of it,” Russell told Sky Sports. “Five second [penalty] cost me two or three positions, but the pace wasn't good enough when it needed to be. I don't know – just not being quick enough. “I need to try and understand why it is. It's strange when you're so far off. Hopefully there's some answers somewhere, but right now I don't have them.” Russell now trails Antonelli by a whopping 123 points with 125 left to play for over the remaining five rounds of the year. “We are very close,” the 20-year-old Italian, who would become the sport’s youngest-ever champion, said after his win in Austin. “We try to finish on a high and hopefully we can clinch it very soon,” Antonelli said. Kimi Antonelli is on the verge of his first world title (Getty) “I am going to approach with the same mindset – to have fun and fight for another win. Would be best to finish well, that’s the goal but just going to try and enjoy the rest of the season. “I am very happy because I have a very good group of people around me in the team and my father who always comes,” Antonelli added. “A great group of people that help me to be more relaxed and not worry about these kind of things, help me to block out the noise and allow me to enjoy the weekend and perform. “On Thursday a lot of talk about championship and stuff and I just try to not worry about that and deliver the best result I could. Today was very important for me and the team.”

item.title: Mourinho keeps Clasico midas touch 13 years on as La Liga heats up
item.description: Real Madrid have now won five consecutive games in all competitions [Getty Images] Jose Mourinho has done it again. The Real Madrid manager celebrated Kylian Mbappe's late winner at Barcelona on Sunday with a trademark knee slide, as he maintained his midas touch over their bitter rivals. Mourinho has become just the third Real boss to go six El Clasicos in a row without defeat - 13 years after he last led Los Blancos in this fixture. Four wins and two draws in his past six matches in charge of Real Madrid against Barcelona put him up there with Miguel Munoz (1962 to 1965) and Vicente del Bosque (2001 to 2003) as Real managers who have gone six in a row without defeat against the old enemy. It was also just a second victory in eight games against Barcelona for Real, with the return of Mourinho to the fixture haunting the reigning champions And more importantly for Mourinho, Mbappe's double in Real's 2-1 win ended Barcelona's nine-game unbeaten domestic run with a crucial Clasico victory at the Camp Nou. A Real defeat would have allowed Barcelona to establish a commanding nine-point advantage but the result has transformed the top of La Liga, bringing Mourinho's side to within three points of their rivals. "In my view, Real Madrid do not play to win at the Camp Nou, Real Madrid play to win La Liga," he said. "We could win with luck, but we won with calmness and with all merit," he said. "It's a very strong group. Everyone works very hard. Everyone was ready to win. "The credit goes to the players. When you win, the credit goes to the players. But when you lose, the blame falls on you. And that's why we see coaches being sacked from their positions every week." The Portuguese, who returned to Real 13 years after his first stint in charge this summer, has now won six and lost six El Clasicos. He said: "I've learned that I have an extraordinary group, with the quality and mindset to play. "In midfield, having a mix of talents gives us more than just having two players with similar characteristics. This mix of talents gives us balance when defending and quality when we go on the attack. "We've beaten several teams by four or more goals, but this is Barca, and the players put on a great performance. We need to continue like this and don't go over the moon after this win." Barcelona boss Hansi Flick said he didn't want to give excuses for the defeat but admitted his team lacked fresh legs after a demanding few weeks. "We missed the freshness," he said. "It's not easy for our players. We have to recover well, train well and we have to respond from this defeat. "In big games, small things are important and they decide the games and today, it wasn't on our side. "I can see that today we were not fresh and this is what we have to change." item.title: Dolphins Accused of Letting Five-Time Pro Bowler’s Career ‘Die’ Through 2018 Browns Trade
item.description: Former Five-time Pro Bowler Jarvis Landry spent four seasons with the Miami Dolphins after they selected him No. 63 overall in the 2014 NFL Draft. Miami placed the franchise tag on the wide receiver in 2018, then traded him to the Cleveland Browns in March of that year for a 2018 fourth-round pick and a 2019 seventh-round pick. Before the trade, Landry made three straight Pro Bowls in South Florida and set an NFL record with 400 receptions through his first four seasons. However, he never wanted to leave. Recently, he called out the Dolphins and former head coach Adam Gase for sending him to Cleveland. Jarvis Landry accuses Adam Gase of trying to end his NFL career Landry’s career did not stall after Gase sent him to the Browns. He caught 81 passes for 976 yards and four touchdowns in his first season in Cleveland and earned a fourth straight Pro Bowl nod. Nov 21, 2021; Cleveland, Ohio, USA; Cleveland Browns running back Nick Chubb (24) celebrates with wide receiver Jarvis Landry (80) after scoring a touchdown during the first half against the Detroit Lions at FirstEnergy Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Ken Blaze-USA TODAY Sports In 2019, he posted a career-high 1,174 receiving yards on 83 receptions and made his fifth consecutive Pro Bowl. But the problem was Cleveland’s record, because they had gone a combined 1-31 in 2016 and 2017. “I did not want to leave from Miami,” Landry said on his 4th and South podcast. “That was a situation with a coach that he just decided that he was going to try to send me to Cleveland and let my career die and be over with. But when we really take a look at it, bro, we was talking numbers of s*** that I had earned.” “Let my career die and be over with.” Jarvis Landry never wanted to leave the Miami Dolphins. The regime at the time had other plans. 3 more Pro Bowls. Almost DOUBLE the numbers. And they still asked him to take a pay cut. #FinsUp #JarvisLandry #NFL #4thAndSouth https://t.co/ueyAsqRzBn — 4th and South (@4thAndSouthPod) October 24, 2026 Initially, Landry’s individual success did little to change Cleveland’s losing culture. Under head coach Hue Jackson and interim coach Gregg Williams, the Browns finished the 2018 season with a 7-8-1 record. The coaching carousel spun the following year again, but under first-time head coach Freddie Kitchens, the Browns regressed to a disappointing 6-10 finish in 2019. Despite the team’s struggles, Landry remained a bright spot, earning Pro Bowl nods in both seasons. The breakthrough finally came in 2020 under a completely new regime. With the hiring of general manager Andrew Berry and first-year head coach Kevin Stefanski, Cleveland’s identity shifted. The Browns surged to an 11-5 record, capturing their first winning season since 2007 and ending a league-high 17-year playoff drought. Landry drove the offense in that season. He missed one game due to COVID-19 protocols but still led the team’s receivers with 72 receptions for 840 yards and three touchdowns in 15 games. Landry

item.title: Seahawks-Chiefs live discussion: Will another unbeaten team lose?
item.description: (Photo by Caleb Bowlin/Getty Images) | Getty Images The undefeated Kansas City Chiefs travel to Seattle to take on Sam Darnold and the Seahawks. The Chiefs will be without WR1 and WR2. They’ll also be without right tackle Jaylon Moore. The last place you want to be is short-handed against this Seahawks defense. We saw how they can prey on teams last year when the 49ers weren’t at full strength. But it’s Patrick Mahomes, and you’re asking for it by doubting him. It’ll be a tall task to come away victorious in Seattle. We saw what it took for the 49ers to win. Will it end differently for the Chiefs? Darnold has thrown an interception in three of the four games since he returned from injury. It would be news if Darnold didn’t turn the ball over at this point. Darnold gets a Chiefs defense that is ninth in the NFL in interception percentage. I see the Seahawks winning comfortably, 24-14, in an ugly game.

item.title: USC football rumors: Trojans brass would ‘welcome’ Lincoln Riley pursuing Baylor job
item.description: Anthony Wahl-Imagn Images USC football rumors: Trojans brass would ‘welcome’ Lincoln Riley pursuing Baylor job appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . With the USC football team losing to the Wisconsin Badgers on Saturday, 24-7, there is no denying that there is a conversation surrounding the job security of head coach Lincoln Riley . While some fans could be demanding that USC football make a change from Riley, this college football insider could be signaling that the coach could trigger a move. The latest from Bruce Feldman of The Athletic comes after the news of Dave Aranda being fired by the Baylor Bears, opening a big college football gig. Feldman would have Riley as the “biggest wild card in this season.” Feldman would even say that if Riley were to be interested in the job, the Trojans “would welcome a move,” adding that he’s a Texas native. “The 43-year-old has a sterling reputation as an offensive coach and for working with QBs. But his five-year run at USC has been so underwhelming, it’s worth asking if he’d like to re-shuffle the deck. We’re pretty confident USC brass would welcome a move like this if Riley is intrigued, especially after the Trojans got mauled this weekend at Wisconsin, where his team was held to minus 17 rushing yards and seven points — fewest ever by a Riley-coached team.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) More on the USC football team this season with Lincoln Riley Despite the USC football program being 6-2 on the season, Feldman claims that the Trojans “hasn’t beaten anything close to a ranked team this season.” With some key games left, Feldman says that aside from Riley winning three of the final four games, “it feels like a stretch that he’ll be able to do enough to convince” the brass at USC that he’s the guy. “The Trojans have games left against Ohio State, at Indiana, a dreadful Maryland team and at UCLA,” Feldman wrote. “His buyout with USC is massive, somewhere around $70 million. Would he be tempted to move back to Texas — and the Big 12?” Riley leads the Trojans against Ohio State on Saturday, as an unranked team beating the Buckeyes could give the fanbase and the school some confidence, though some may believe his exit is inevitable. Related: Why Texas A&M football’s Mike Elko didn’t bench Marcel Reed after brutal pick-six vs. Alabama Related: UCLA HC Bob Chesney breathes a sigh of relief on Wayne Knight injury scare

item.title: Oregon Fires First-Year Offensive Coordinator Amid Disappointing Season
item.description: Oregon Ducks has fired its offensive coordinator following the team’s 21-10 loss to Illinois on October 24. The decision came after the Ducks struggled to produce points in three consecutive games. Oregon’s offense has scored no more than 17 points in each of those three games, with the Ducks losing to UCLA and Illinois while recording a win over Nebraska. Oregon dismisses offensive coordinator after Illinois loss Oregon has fired offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer following its 21-10 loss to Illinois on Saturday. On3 reporter Pete Nakos reported the decision. The Ducks hold a 4-3 overall record and a 2-2 mark in Big Ten play. Oregon Ducks head coach Dan Lanning, left, talks to Oregon Ducks offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer before the game as the Oregon Ducks host the Nebraska Cornhuskers on Oct. 17, 2026, at Autzen Stadium in Eugene, Oregon. Oregon produced 42 total points across its last three games. The Ducks lost to UCLA, defeated Nebraska and then fell to Illinois. Against Illinois, Oregon led 10-0 at halftime but did not score again. Illinois scored 21 unanswered points to win 21-10. The Ducks finished with 426 total yards but converted just four of 15 third-down attempts. After the loss, Nakos reported the move in a social media post, writing : “Oregon has dismissed offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer.” Quarterback Dylan Raiola completed 27 of 41 passes for 246 yards against Illinois. Running back Jordon Davison recorded 92 rushing yards, while Dierre Hill added 83. Wide receiver Dakorien Moore caught nine passes for 70 yards. Oregon has also played without starting quarterback Dante Moore for three consecutive games. Moore suffered a concussion against USC, leaving Dylan Raiola and Brock Thomas to handle quarterback duties during his absence. Mehringer joined head coach Dan Lanning’s staff in January 2022 as the team’s tight ends coach. He later became co-offensive coordinator while continuing to coach tight ends. For the 2026 season, he took over as Oregon’s full-time offensive coordinator after Will Stein left the program to become Kentucky’s head coach. During the 2025 season, when Mehringer served as co-offensive coordinator, Oregon averaged 36.9 points and 452.2 total yards per game. Lanning announced Mehringer’s departure in an official statement on October 25. He thanked Mehringer for his work with the program, acknowledged his contributions over several seasons and said he believed the offense needed a new direction. Lanning said , “This was a decision I felt was in the best interest of our football program, as I believe a new direction is necessary to move our offense forward.” Oregon has not announced who will replace Mehringer as offensive coordinator or take over offensive play-calling duties. The Ducks are scheduled to host Northwestern at Autzen Stadium on October 31. Their remaining regular-season opponents also include Ohio State, Michigan, Michigan State and Washington. More College Football News Dan Lanning Confirm

Oregon Ducks head coach Dan Lanning, left, talks to Oregon Ducks offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer before the game as the Oregon Ducks host the Nebraska Cornhuskers on Oct. 17, 2026, at Autzen Stadium in Eugene, Oregon. Oregon produced 42 total points across its last three games. The Ducks lost to UCLA, defeated Nebraska and then fell to Illinois. Against Illinois, Oregon led 10-0 at halftime but did not score again. Illinois scored 21 unanswered points to win 21-10. The Ducks finished with 426 total yards but converted just four of 15 third-down attempts. After the loss, Nakos reported the move in a social media post, writing : “Oregon has dismissed offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer.” Quarterback Dylan Raiola completed 27 of 41 passes for 246 yards against Illinois. Running back Jordon Davison recorded 92 rushing yards, while Dierre Hill added 83. Wide receiver Dakorien Moore caught nine passes for 70 yards. Oregon has also played without starting quarterback Dante Moore for three consecutive games. Moore suffered a concussion against USC, leaving Dylan Raiola and Brock Thomas to handle quarterback duties during his absence. Mehringer joined head coach Dan Lanning’s staff in January 2022 as the team’s tight ends coach. He later became co-offensive coordinator while continuing to coach tight ends. For the 2026 season, he took over as Oregon’s full-time offensive coordinator after Will Stein left the program to become Kentucky’s head coach. During the 2025 season, when Mehringer served as co-offensive coordinator, Oregon averaged 36.9 points and 452.2 total yards per game. Lanning announced Mehringer’s departure in an official statement on October 25. He thanked Mehringer for his work with the program, acknowledged his contributions over several seasons and said he believed the offense needed a new direction. Lanning said , “This was a decision I felt was in the best interest of our football program, as I believe a new direction is necessary to move our offense forward.” Oregon has not announced who will replace Mehringer as offensive coordinator or take over offensive play-calling duties. The Ducks are scheduled to host Northwestern at Autzen Stadium on October 31. Their remaining regular-season opponents also include Ohio State, Michigan, Michigan State and Washington. item.title: Rams-Raiders takeaways: Sean McVay finally leans into run game
item.description: The Los Angeles Rams entered their Week 7 matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders needing a convincing performance to regain momentum, and the result offered plenty to evaluate on both sides of the football. From Stafford’s command of the offense to the ground game’s effectiveness and the defense’s ability to control the Raiders in the first half, here are the biggest takeaways from the Rams’ Week 7 35-21 win over the Las Vegas Raiders . 1st Down: Matthew Stafford is now Rams all time TD leader Stafford’s three touchdowns in the first half officially made him the all-time passing touchdown leader for the Rams franchise. Stafford’s record breaking moment puts in a category of his own. He is now first all-time for both the Lions and Rams organizations. His 156 touchdown passes surpassed Roman Gabriel, who played 11 years with the Rams from 1962-1972. 🚨 NFL HISTORY Matthew Stafford is the FIRST quarterback in NFL history to hold the all-time passing touchdown record for TWO different franchise! Detroit Lions- 282 Los Angeles Rams- 155 pic.twitter.com/cgzSKxkZMU — Novig (@Novig) October 25, 2026 2nd Down: Rams lean into run game Through the first six weeks of the season, Los Angeles was throwing the ball about 65% of the time. The game plan was different this Sunday as Kyren Williams and Blake Corum were given 33 rushing attempts and worked that to the tune of 192 rushing yards. It was a huge effort to get the ground game going and make the LA offense multi-dimensional again. Rams offense with a casual 75% success rate on offense against the Raiders. If it holds, that’s the highest success rate by any team since 2016 ( @NextGenStats era) — Asa (@AsaArnold4) October 25, 2026 3rd Down: Rams 3 tight ends come up big The Rams trio of tight ends combined for 11 receptions, 82 receiving yards, and two touchdowns. Colby Parkinson led the group with 5 receptions and 48 yards. Davis Allen collected the first two touchdowns and nearly added a third. As for Higbee, he hauled in a huge third down conversion to prevent any thought of a Raiders comeback. What a throw by Matthew Stafford and catch by Tyler Higbee 🔥 LARvsLV on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/6p15WoLfO0 — NFL (@NFL) October 25, 2026 4th Down: Defense was good enough In the first half, the defense was stout. The interior defensive line was a stout despite being without Kobie Turner and Poona Ford. Aaron Donald, Ty Hamilton, and Braden Fiske held the Raiders to 48 rushing yards on 17 rushing attempts (2.8 per attempt). The secondary forced multiple incompletions including three 4th down stops. Things got a little dicey because of some sloppiness on the offensive side and putting the defense in short fields. Despite being without 4 defensive starters, the Rams defense got the job done with a few backups like Shaun Dolac and Emmanuel Forbes being good enough in the win.

item.title: Big 12 Coach Explains Why He Donated $2 Million to His Own Football Program
item.description: The Utah football coach and his wife, Liz, donated to the program, explaining their decision to give back to the university. The coach said the university had given a great deal to his family, which has longstanding ties to the institution. His father played football for Utah, he played safety for the Utes, and his wife also attended the university. Family ties drive donation to support Utah Football’s future Utah Utes head coach Morgan Scalley has made it clear he wants to stay at the university . He and his wife, Liz, committed $2 million to the football program, a donation announced on March 12, 2026. During his October 23 appearance on The Pat McAfee Show, Scalley explained that the decision reflected his family’s longstanding ties to the university and their desire to give back. Jul 8, 2026; Frisco, TX, USA; Utah head coach Morgan Scalley speaks to reporters during Big 12 Conference Football Media Days at The Star. Mandatory Credit: Raymond Carlin III-Imagn Images Morgan Scalley said the decision stemmed from his connection to the university. He grew up in Salt Lake City’s Sugar House neighborhood, played safety for the Utes, and remains closely connected to the university Explaining the family’s reasons for making the donation, Scalley said : “Utah’s done a ton for me and my family. My wife went here. My entire family went to the University of Utah. There’s a lot the Utah family has given us. This is not a Morgan Scalley thing. I said that early on. It’s about Utah football. It’s about the University of Utah. When I’m gone, again, it’ll still be Utah. We wanted to give back and help this community understand that we’re in this together. I’m not going anywhere unless they kick me out of here.” Scalley said the contribution was intended to support Utah football and the wider university community rather than focus on him personally. He said the gift reflected the family’s connection to the university The donation comes during a period of significant change in college athletics, including NIL opportunities and revenue-sharing arrangements. These developments have reshaped the college football landscape. The $2 million gift is intended to support the Utah football program’s long-term success, although the university has not specified how the money will be allocated. Scalley has spent much of his coaching career with the program. He joined Utah as an administrative assistant in 2006, became a graduate assistant in 2007 and took over as safeties coach in 2008. From 2009 through 2015, he served as recruiting coordinator. He also assumed special teams responsibilities in 2015. In 2016, Scalley became defensive coordinator and remained in the position through the 2025 season. The university appointed him head coach in December 2025, succeeding Kyle Whittingham. item.title: SEC Program Gets $500K Payback One Week After Its Own Field Storm vs. Alabama
item.description: Shane Beamer spent most of October answering questions about his future at South Carolina. Then the Gamecocks went to Gainesville on October 10 and beat then-No. 16 Florida 38-19, ending an eight-game SEC losing streak. A bye week followed, and a ranked SEC visitor was waiting in Columbia. What unfolded gave Beamer a night to remember, but it also came with a costly catch. South Carolina faces $500K SEC fine after Tennessee upset South Carolina stunned No. 11 Tennessee 27-24 at Williams-Brice Stadium on Saturday night. Malik Orsan’s 48-yard field goal sailed through as time expired, and thousands of fans poured onto the field . The South Carolina Gamecocks (4-3, 2-3 SEC) built a 14-0 lead, but Tennessee scored 21 points in the second quarter and later led 24-17. With 3:35 left, the Vols went for it on fourth-and-1 from the South Carolina 39 and were stopped. Quarterback LaNorris Sellers made them pay. He fought through two defenders on third-and-goal, and the tying touchdown stood after review with 1:17 left. He ran for 96 yards and two scores. Beamer praised Sellers. “He’s freakin unbelievable,” Beamer said afterword. “The play he made to score that touchdown. Unreal, one of the great plays probably in the history of South Carolina football.” Oct 10, 2026; Gainesville, Florida, USA; South Carolina Gamecocks head coach Shane Beamer looks on before a game against the Florida Gators at Ben Hill Griffin Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Matt Pendleton-Imagn Images Dylan Stewart then sacked George MacIntyre and forced a fumble with 33 seconds left. Tomiwa Durojaiye recovered at the Tennessee 34, setting up Orsan’s winner. Under the SEC’s access-to-competition-area policy, every field storm now carries a flat $500,000 fine, paid to the visiting school. Tennessee paid the same amount a week earlier after its fans stormed the field following a win over Alabama. The league has not yet announced this penalty, but it is expected. Now the spotlight shifts to Beamer, whose future looked far different three weeks ago. Shane Beamer’s job security was in doubt three weeks ago Three weeks earlier, the mood around Beamer was bleak. South Carolina blew a 17-0 lead and lost 35-34 in overtime to Kentucky on October 3, extending its SEC losing streak to eight games. Fans voiced their anger, and buyout talk grew louder. Asked about his standing, he pointed to the support he had been getting. “I don’t know anything other than what they’ve told me, that they’ve been super-supportive,” Beamer told reporters. “And have been all along. Wish we could have put a better result on the field tonight.” A report suggested that, Beamer’s job appeared safe before the Florida game , with a bye week viewed as a potential window for a coaching change. Instead, the Gamecocks won in Gainesville, took their bye, and beat ranked Tennessee at home. item.title: ‘Edgy’ Arch Manning is a better leader, but still mistake-prone
item.description: AUSTIN, TEXAS - OCTOBER 24: Arch Manning #16 of the Texas Longhorns reacts in the first quarter against the Ole Miss Rebels at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium on October 24, 2026 in Austin, Texas. (Photo by Tim Warner/Getty Images) | Getty Images AUSTIN — Does Texas Longhorns head coach Steve Sarkisian want to see senior quarterback Arch Manning make his “edgy” personality more permanent? “Yeah, love it,” Sarkisian responded. “That fires me up.” Similar to Manning’s wild vascillation between high-level plays and confounding errors and turn downs , Manning’s personality also swings, from quiet and withdrawn to swaggy and fiery as his confidence ebbs and flows. On Saturday, Texas got the edgy version in a 34-27 victory over Ole Miss in the wake of back-to-back losses to unranked opponents that saw Manning commit late, game-changing turnovers in both games after week-long speculation swirled about the possibility of Sarkisian taking the rare step of benching his starter . Sarkisian met personally with Manning last Sunday to challenge his highly-touted quarterback. During the week, Manning’s edgy personality emerged. Or re-emerged, depending on the perspective . Remember the shit-talking leader from preseason camp ? “He’s edgy right now, and honestly, I appreciate that about him,” Sarkisian said Thursday. “At some point, he’s got to fight back, and the best way for him to fight back is going out and playing really good football with his teammates and enjoy playing football with his teammates, so I’m looking forward to watching him compete Saturday night.” Over recent weeks, Texas has struggled to translate how players practice into how players play , but Manning did at least take the edginess with which he operated during the week into the Ole Miss game, elevated by his first two rushing touchdowns of the season. The first, a two-yard run at the end of the first quarter, not only gave the Longhorns a seven-point lead, it also provided an indelible image of Manning’s celebration synced perfectly to the heightened experience at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium. Victory Sunday🤘 pic.twitter.com/TFKgvdLXNW — Texas Football (@TexasFootball) October 25, 2026 A sideline shot captured the type of fire that has defined the best moments of Manning’s Texas tenure. In his worst moments, the absence of it has left a tangible void. "I'm coming. I'm fucking coming." pic.twitter.com/aHsey6Snq0 — JM Football (@JomboyMediaFB) October 25, 2026 Quantifying the points added or lost by the difference in Manning’s leadership is impossible, but the result on Saturday compared to the results the previous two weeks affords some data points, at least. In between the whistles, the Arch Manning Experience hit some all-too-familiar beats while showing some signs of progress. item.content:encoded: AUSTIN, TEXAS - OCTOBER 24: Arch Manning #16 of the Texas Longhorns reacts in the first quarter against the Ole Miss Rebels at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium on October 24, 2026 in Austin, Texas. (Photo by Tim Warner/Getty Images) | Getty Images AUSTIN — Does Texas Longhorns head coach Steve Sarkisian want to see senior quarterback Arch Manning make his “edgy” personality more permanent? “Yeah, love it,” Sarkisian responded. “That fires me up.” Similar to Manning’s wild vascillation between high-level plays and confounding errors and turn downs , Manning’s personality also swings, from quiet and withdrawn to swaggy and fiery as his confidence ebbs and flows. On Saturday, Texas got the edgy version in a 34-27 victory over Ole Miss in the wake of back-to-back losses to unranked opponents that saw Manning commit late, game-changing turnovers in both games after week-long speculation swirled about the possibility of Sarkisian taking the rare step of benching his starter . Sarkisian met personally with Manning last Sunday to challenge his highly-touted quarterback. During the week, Manning’s edgy personality emerged. Or re-emerged, depending on the perspective . Remember the shit-talking leader from preseason camp ? “He’s edgy right now, and honestly, I appreciate that about him,” Sarkisian said Thursday. “At some point, he’s got to fight back, and the best way for him to fight back is going out and playing really good football with his teammates and enjoy playing football with his teammates, so I’m looking forward to watching him compete Saturday night.” Over recent weeks, Texas has struggled to translate how players practice into how players play , but Manning did at least take the edginess with which he operated during the week into the Ole Miss game, elevated by his first two rushing touchdowns of the season. The first, a two-yard run at the end of the first quarter, not only gave the Longhorns a seven-point lead, it also provided an indelible image of Manning’s celebration synced perfectly to the heightened experience at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium. Victory Sunday🤘 pic.twitter.com/TFKgvdLXNW — Texas Football (@TexasFootball) October 25, 2026 A sideline shot captured the type of fire that has defined the best moments of Manning’s Texas tenure. In his worst moments, the absence of it has left a tangible void. "I'm coming. I'm fucking coming." pic.twitter.com/aHsey6Snq0 — JM Football (@JomboyMediaFB) October 25, 2026 Quantifying the points added or lost by the difference in Manning’s leadership is impossible, but the result on Saturday compared to the results the previous two weeks affords some data points, at least. In between the whistles, the Arch Manning Experience hit some all-too-familiar beats while showing some signs of progress. The combination of Sarkisian calling more routes over the middle, where Manning is hyper efficient, and the Texas quarterback operating with less hesitancy, an issue that contributed to multiple sacks in last week’s loss to Florida, helped the Longhorns race out to a 24-3 lead at halftime on 13-of-19 passing for 171 yards, including a beautiful 50-yard touchdown pass to junior wide receiver Ryan Wingo. ARCH MANNING TO RYAN WINGO BLURRRR pic.twitter.com/xdOUq9bUpU — wok (@wokdior) October 25, 2026 The throw to Wingo was the weekly pinnacle for Manning. Other decisions ended poorly when Manning admittedly didn’t see the defenders who intercepted two of his passes, but at least happened with less hesitancy? The first came on the type of out route to junior wide receiver Emmett Mosley that Manning missed consistently against the Gators. On the second Texas drive, Ole Miss busted its coverage, leaving two defenders on Mosley as junior wide receiver Ryan Wingo came open on a corner route. ARCH MANNING IS PICKED OFF BY JALYN CRAWFORD pic.twitter.com/L0GeUsNoyb — ClutchWire (@ClutchWireHQ) October 25, 2026 The second interception was more confounding when Manning threw into triple coverage trying to target sophomore tight end Emaree Winston deep down the field. arch manning interception; ole miss vs texas pic.twitter.com/kSFGeaDzuy — ◇ (@F0RGIAT0) October 25, 2026 Of Winston’s six receptions this season, only one has come more than 10 yards down the field. Manning’s inability to layer a pass to Winston in another instance is reflective of his regular misfires, albeit one made more difficult by having to reset his feet after moving out of the pocket and throwing across the field. If Arch Manning starts to dial in these throws, he's going to be very hard to defend He's looking like the QB we saw last year pic.twitter.com/uSrPAh8J6M — Nash (@NashTalksTexas) October 25, 2026 Manning’s other turnover, the sack-fumble on the first drive of the third quarter, wasn’t primarily his fault because backup left tackle Andre Cojoe got beat badly on a speed rush. OLE MISS FORCES A FUMBLE AND SCORES THEIR FIRST TOUCHDOWN ARCH MANNING WITH THE FUMBLE pic.twitter.com/EhEUkLtfEA — ClutchWire (@ClutchWireHQ) October 25, 2026 After another game of highs and lows, Manning and the Longhorns broke their losing streak, and the embattled quarterback shared an emotional moment on the field with his family. All smiles 🤠 pic.twitter.com/rQDWE6cuTj — Texas Football (@TexasFootball) October 25, 2026 Meeting with the media after the game, Manning provided some further insight into why that moment was so important to him. “Probably because it was a hard Sunday and I went over to their place and damn near bawl cried to them, so just being able to see them after a game, after a win, felt good,” Manning said. Years of hype built up the expectations surrounding the big, speedy quarterback with the famous last name who seemingly had all the attributes to excel at Texas. Now Manning is reveling in his newfound existence on the opposite end of the spectrum. “I think I kind of like being disregarded and counted out,” Manning said. Like Manning said on Monday, he’s going to die on the hill of letting it rip . That’s the plan, at least.

item.title: Hamilton Reveals Friday Data Deficit Behind Ferrari Teammate Leclerc’s US GP Podium
item.description: Lewis Hamilton reveals what he lacked when compared to Charles Leclerc to lose out at the F1 US GP, where a front wing adjustment cost him hugely. Ferrari ’s Hamilton ended up fourth in the F1 US GP at the Circuit of the Americas, just about a second off the podium from Red Bull’s Max Verstappen . Teammate Charles Leclerc was second, and the Brit knows the difference that made it happen. It goes back to Friday when Hamilton started the F1 US GP weekend on the wrong foot and lost valuable time in FP1 and also FP2. It allowed Leclerc to accumulate the data and learning that ultimately made the difference on Sunday. Hamilton Understood his F1 US GP Problems From Get Go Hamilton complained that he couldn’t turn the car, which is where he started to lose time. “I was lacking pace in the first two stints basically,” he said to the media after the F1 US GP. “I just couldn’t turn the car. And I think ultimately it all kind of started on Friday. Wrong setup, really, for FP1 and then went the wrong direction in FP2. “Reverted back and got to a better place for FP3. But there’s a subtle difference between Charles and our car, basically just in the race, and it’s mostly just to do with the flap for how much wing you put on, and I think we’ve just been under-hitting it. Continuously under-hitting it for some reason. “And when you do the lap to the grid, it feels like the car is good and then as soon as the race starts, massive washout and understeer, and I couldn’t do anything about it, so they just pulled away. I lost those eight seconds, and that’s really why I didn’t get that position in the end,” summed up Hamilton . Hamilton Explains How He Got it Sorted at the Pit Stops How did he manage to have a better end? It was said on the radio. Hamilton wanted to adjust the front wing flap, which is what Ferrari did in the two pit stops. But he was still short by the end of it. That ultimately led to his downer, as he did not have the experience that Leclerc managed to gain in practice. “Because through the pit stops, I added four clicks,” said Hamilton. “Next, at the next pit stop, I added another four clicks, and even then, I’m still another four clicks too short. And it’s crazy to be 12 clicks down; we really need to look at how we get to that point. item.content:encoded: Lewis Hamilton reveals what he lacked when compared to Charles Leclerc to lose out at the F1 US GP, where a front wing adjustment cost him hugely. Ferrari ’s Hamilton ended up fourth in the F1 US GP at the Circuit of the Americas, just about a second off the podium from Red Bull’s Max Verstappen . Teammate Charles Leclerc was second, and the Brit knows the difference that made it happen. It goes back to Friday when Hamilton started the F1 US GP weekend on the wrong foot and lost valuable time in FP1 and also FP2. It allowed Leclerc to accumulate the data and learning that ultimately made the difference on Sunday. Hamilton Understood his F1 US GP Problems From Get Go Hamilton complained that he couldn’t turn the car, which is where he started to lose time. “I was lacking pace in the first two stints basically,” he said to the media after the F1 US GP. “I just couldn’t turn the car. And I think ultimately it all kind of started on Friday. Wrong setup, really, for FP1 and then went the wrong direction in FP2. “Reverted back and got to a better place for FP3. But there’s a subtle difference between Charles and our car, basically just in the race, and it’s mostly just to do with the flap for how much wing you put on, and I think we’ve just been under-hitting it. Continuously under-hitting it for some reason. “And when you do the lap to the grid, it feels like the car is good and then as soon as the race starts, massive washout and understeer, and I couldn’t do anything about it, so they just pulled away. I lost those eight seconds, and that’s really why I didn’t get that position in the end,” summed up Hamilton . Hamilton Explains How He Got it Sorted at the Pit Stops How did he manage to have a better end? It was said on the radio. Hamilton wanted to adjust the front wing flap, which is what Ferrari did in the two pit stops. But he was still short by the end of it. That ultimately led to his downer, as he did not have the experience that Leclerc managed to gain in practice. “Because through the pit stops, I added four clicks,” said Hamilton. “Next, at the next pit stop, I added another four clicks, and even then, I’m still another four clicks too short. And it’s crazy to be 12 clicks down; we really need to look at how we get to that point. But I think it would have been a bit different if we had started with it, I think, in FP2, where you did in the long run. “That’s where Charles got the experience in that setup, and I didn’t get the long run on it, so instead of being on the back foot, but with lots of positives to take, the team seemed to do a really great job with pit stops and strategy, and we obviously had a decent pace today, particularly last stint. “If I had that in the first two, it would have for sure been in the for sure, been on the podium, I think in the end,” summed up Hamilton, who felt the tire strategy went wrong on his end once again. It was not the strategy in itself but the choice of compound. Ultimately, the hard tire was the best of the lot. Hamilton Felt Hard Tyre was the Best Compound He had saved two sets of medium tires, which didn’t work as well as expected. He thought he made a good start to pounce on ailing Verstappen, but starting on the used soft tire cost him better pace. “Yeah, I mean, I chose to have two medium tires because they didn’t think the hard tire was going to be any good,” continued Hamilton. “In hindsight, it would have been two hard tires, which would have been the better one. The hard tire was the best tire. And then it meant I started on a used soft, which is from used to new; it’s two seconds of race time. And so, it affects the start as well compared to others that are on the new. “All the cars ahead are on the new, but I had a really good start, nearly got to third place or whatever it was, but Charles was on the outside, and I didn’t get to capitalize on that. But yeah, otherwise, as I said, there are lots of positives to take from it. I think lots of learning. “I think if, for the next races, I can really get on top of this balance issue that I have, I think we can get much better results. If I had the balance that I need, even if I just had the balancing of the last stint, I would have been right in the fight all the way to the end, but I think even then, another step from there, I think we could have probably qualified better. And so, some good points.” Lewis Hamilton | Photo Credit: Scuderia Ferrari VSC Cost a Podium Chance But Issue was First Two Stints As pointed out earlier, Hamilton managed to gain massively on the last stint on the hard compound. He got through Lando Norris and had Verstappen in his sights. But a late Virtual Safety Car period potentially cost him laps and time. Ultimately, the first two stints cost him that extra time, which was the difference he had to make. “I think, well, we have got to have a little bit of a battle with Max in the last couple of laps, so, yeah, that would have been awesome,” said Hamilton. “But as I said, I think it was all the first two stints; I just lost so much ground. Can’t be giving up that time in the future. I think I really feel like I’m happy with how I drove. “It took two whole stints to try and get this car to turn, and then once it started to turn in the third stint, I was back on pace with the guys ahead and had a big gap to close — eight or nine seconds or whatever it was — to the car ahead. So those guys are obviously very quick, so I just got to work on not losing that second points,” summed up Hamilton.

item.title: Peyton Manning’s Role in Colts GM Search Clarified After Chris Ballard Firing
item.description: Peyton Manning is one of the greatest players, if not the greatest, to ever play for the Indianapolis Colts . The former quarterback is one of the most decorated players in American football history. He has won the Super Bowl two times, and is a five-time NFL Most Valuable Player. The Colts have not found the same success since Manning’s departure. He has now taken an important decision regarding his former team. Peyton Manning not expected to take Colts GM role The Colts recently fired general manager Chris Ballard after more than nine seasons. While in charge at the franchise, the team had a 72-82-1 record, made two playoff appearances, and started 14 different quarterbacks after Andrew Luck’s retirement. Owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon has said the franchise will conduct a thorough search for the next general manager. One of the names initially linked to the search was none other than Manning. Oct 19, 2025; Denver, Colorado, USA; Peyton Manning looks on before the game between the Denver Broncos and New York Giants at Empower Field at Mile High. Mandatory Credit: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images However, according to league sources cited by ESPN’s Adam Schefter , the legendary quarterback is not expected to emerge as a candidate for the Colts’ vacant general manager position. The franchise have not contacted Manning about the role, and the Hall of Fame quarterback is not anticipated to pursue it. Manning has not prepared for or expressed interest in becoming an NFL general manager. His post-playing career includes running Omaha Productions, co-hosting the ManningCast on ESPN’s Monday Night Football package, and handling commercial commitments. He also has two children in high school, further limiting time for a position that demands full-time, day-to-day operational focus. Sources indicated the timing is unsuitable given these existing responsibilities. The same sources also said that Manning remains open to considering NFL opportunities in the future, but only for those that involve higher-profile executive or ownership-adjacent roles similar to those held by other former players. Some examples include Tom Brady’s role as minority owner and adviser with the Las Vegas Raiders, Matt Ryan as president of football for the Atlanta Falcons, and Tony Boselli as executive vice president of football operations for the Jacksonville Jaguars. Manning has previously talked about leading an NFL team from the front office. Peyton Manning once spoke about running football team Manning previously shared his thoughts on running a football team in the future. In an interview with the Denver Post , he said, “I don’t think that’s anywhere on my radar by any means. I love being an ambassador for the Broncos and for the Colts, for the University of Tennessee.
