item.title: End approaching for Carrick but Man Utd fans make clear who they blame
item.description: There was an air of inevitability about Michael Carrick's walk around Old Trafford after the 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth. It is not unusual for Carrick to applaud the Manchester United fans. If anything, his acknowledgements were not as pronounced as they were in Como after the equally devastating loss. But after eight games without a win, the worst run since 2015-16 and two horrific defeats in a week, the end is approaching for Carrick, with his bosses in serious talks about his future. However, if anyone in a senior position at the club thinks the issues at Old Trafford will be solved simply by changing the head coach and, more importantly, the fans will be appeased by a new face in the dugout, the reaction from the stands on an awful day on and off the pitch would have very clearly told them otherwise. On Friday, as he looked back on that 4-1 loss to Como and ahead to Bournemouth, Carrick said: "We'll be a different team on Sunday. We have to be a different team on Sunday." Sadly, they weren't. Carrick could not answer if he will still be in charge for next Saturday's trip to Chelsea. He does not know. "The responsibility is mine," he said. "What else can I say really right now? I totally understand the situation. I'm not expecting anything either way. I love this place and I'll always do what I feel is going to be the best for the football club." Fernandes left on bench for Man Utd defeat - a failed gamble? Carrick future under major threat - can he survive? Third dismissal in three seasons won't reflect well on anyone United's fans delivered their own verdict on the performance as Carrick disappeared down the tunnel to the dressing room. After repeatedly singing the former midfielder's name, as soon as he was out of view they turned on the players. The booing lasted until the last of them, Diogo Dalot, left the pitch. They simply feel they are either not good enough or don't care enough, or both. But there was more, much more. The game was less than a minute old when the first anti-Glazer and anti-Sir Jim Ratcliffe songs were heard. The Glazer family have been public enemy number one among the United faithful ever since their leveraged takeover in 2005. The debt they initially landed on the club has now grown to over £1.15bn, according to their latest accounts. The amount it has cost in interest is £852m, according to respected football finance blogger Swiss Ramble. item.content:encoded: There was an air of inevitability about Michael Carrick's walk around Old Trafford after the 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth. It is not unusual for Carrick to applaud the Manchester United fans. If anything, his acknowledgements were not as pronounced as they were in Como after the equally devastating loss. But after eight games without a win, the worst run since 2015-16 and two horrific defeats in a week, the end is approaching for Carrick, with his bosses in serious talks about his future. However, if anyone in a senior position at the club thinks the issues at Old Trafford will be solved simply by changing the head coach and, more importantly, the fans will be appeased by a new face in the dugout, the reaction from the stands on an awful day on and off the pitch would have very clearly told them otherwise. On Friday, as he looked back on that 4-1 loss to Como and ahead to Bournemouth, Carrick said: "We'll be a different team on Sunday. We have to be a different team on Sunday." Sadly, they weren't. Carrick could not answer if he will still be in charge for next Saturday's trip to Chelsea. He does not know. "The responsibility is mine," he said. "What else can I say really right now? I totally understand the situation. I'm not expecting anything either way. I love this place and I'll always do what I feel is going to be the best for the football club." Fernandes left on bench for Man Utd defeat - a failed gamble? Carrick future under major threat - can he survive? Third dismissal in three seasons won't reflect well on anyone United's fans delivered their own verdict on the performance as Carrick disappeared down the tunnel to the dressing room. After repeatedly singing the former midfielder's name, as soon as he was out of view they turned on the players. The booing lasted until the last of them, Diogo Dalot, left the pitch. They simply feel they are either not good enough or don't care enough, or both. But there was more, much more. The game was less than a minute old when the first anti-Glazer and anti-Sir Jim Ratcliffe songs were heard. The Glazer family have been public enemy number one among the United faithful ever since their leveraged takeover in 2005. The debt they initially landed on the club has now grown to over £1.15bn, according to their latest accounts. The amount it has cost in interest is £852m, according to respected football finance blogger Swiss Ramble. In the last financial year, the interest payment was £37m, an increase from £34m the previous year. The argument is, that money could have been used far more productively to sign better players. There had been hope Ratcliffe, a boyhood United fan, would change that when he struck a deal with the Glazers to become a minority shareholder on Christmas Eve 2023. Instead, a succession of decisions have led to major questions over his handling of the club. On the management side, United's hierarchy eventually backed Erik ten Hag after talking with alternatives in the wake of the shock 2024 FA Cup final triumph over Manchester City, spending over £200m on the likes of Leny Yoro, Matthijs de Ligt and Manuel Ugarte. Last week, Ten Hag told the Athletic the club went back on a promise not to sell homegrown Scotland international Scott McTominay to fund Ugarte's £50m move from Paris St-Germain. They sacked the Dutchman in October 2024. After that they persuaded Ruben Amorim to leave Sporting mid-season, when he wanted to wait until the summer. They stuck with him after an unprecedented 15th-place finish, and again after United lost to League Two Grimsby in the EFL Cup, then sacked him in January when he clashed with director of football Jason Wilcox over playing style. That led to Carrick's arrival to the end of the season, which turned into a permanent appointment after he guided the club back into the Champions League after a two-year absence. A third dismissal in three seasons would not reflect well on anyone. The 'Standards' banner that was held up on the Stretford End showing the images of legendary skippers Bryan Robson, Eric Cantona and Roy Keane was there to remind the executives running the club of the history they should be aspiring to. Manchester United fans unfurled a 'Standards' banner during the 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth, showing the images of three legendary captains Bryan Robson, Eric Cantona and Roy Keane [Getty Images] Recruitment, tickets, new stadium - more reasons why some fans are annoyed Wilcox has largely operated behind the scenes but he could not fail to hear the obscenities being sung against him during today's game, nor the boos as he climbed into the vehicle taking him away from the stadium nearly two hours after the final whistle. Recruited from a similar role at Southampton following the Ratcliffe takeover and elevated in status following the dismissal of Dan Ashworth, amid the decision to recruit Amorim, the 55-year-old is blamed by many fans for the club's recent recruitment, even though the budget was set at a much higher level. Sat next to him at Old Trafford to watch the Bournemouth debacle unfold was chief executive Omar Berrada, who worked with Wilcox at Manchester City. Having senior figures steeped in City's recent history was always a potential problem if results didn't go well. Berrada played no part in the recent Premier League proceedings that found City guilty of multiple breaches of financial rules, but the link is clear, and United's fans sang about that at Old Trafford as well. If that wasn't enough, a ticket touting investigation launched in the summer led to condemnation from all United's major fan groups. The club argued they were trying to catch touts, while fans felt it was an attempt to drive regular match-goers out in favour of more corporate sales. The club are adamant that is not the case, but the argument is falling on deaf ears. The same is also true of plans for a new 100,000-capacity stadium. The club conducted a survey which they said showed the majority of respondents were in favour of a new ground. The stadium is likely to cost in excess of £2bn and United spent £63.5m on land for it earlier this year. Some supporters simply don't believe those figures. The Stretford End impolitely told Ratcliffe they had no interest in a new stadium as well today. Carrick may take responsibility for poor results but there is far more than that causing unrest at Manchester United just now. Manchester United chief executive Omar Berrada (left) sat next to director of football Jason Wilcox for the 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth [Getty Images] Bournemouth beat Man Utd to increase pressure on Carrick Fernandes left out - Man Utd hammered, Bournemouth brilliant - how they rated

item.title: Seahawks’ Kenneth Walker Decision Draws ‘Punch Himself’ Criticism Ahead of Chiefs Matchup
item.description: The Seattle Seahawks enter Sunday night still stinging from a 17-14 overtime loss to the Denver Broncos on Oct. 15, where Sam Darnold was sacked five times and the offense managed just three points on its first eight drives. Now the unbeaten Kansas City Chiefs are coming to town, and amid the Seahawks’ growing running back crisis, general manager John Schneider is facing sharp criticism over one offseason call. Richie Incognito Calls out John Schneider over Kenneth Walker exit Former NFL offensive lineman Richie Incognito did not hold back on his Initial Contact podcast. He pointed straight at Seattle’s rushing attack and the man who built it. “..I think the biggest factor for Seattle is they have absolutely no run game,” Richie Incognito said. “They got the Chiefs coming into their house, and they can look across that sideline at the Super Bowl MVP and John Schneider, the GM of the Seattle Seahawks, should punch himself in the n*** for not even making an offer for this guy.” Oct 11, 2026; Seattle, Washington, USA; Seattle Seahawks general manager John Schneider looks on before a game against the San Francisco 49ers at Lumen Field. Now the unbeaten Kansas City Chiefs are coming to town, and amid the Seahawks’ growing running back crisis, general manager John Schneider is facing sharp criticism over one offseason call. The move has paid off quickly. Walker leads the NFL with 665 rushing yards and six touchdowns through five games, despite the Chiefs’ bye week. item.title: Dan Campbell Explains Controversial Fourth-Down Decision That Nearly Cost Lions vs. Packers
item.description: The Detroit Lions escaped Ford Field with a thrilling 20-17 victory over the Green Bay Packers on Sunday, but head coach Dan Campbell nearly watched one of his trademark aggressive decisions turn a huge NFC North win into a devastating loss. With the game tied late in the fourth quarter, Campbell elected to go for it on fourth-and-1 from Detroit’s own 22-yard line, a decision that immediately backfired. Rather than punt the football and trust a defense that had played exceptionally well throughout the afternoon, Campbell kept his offense on the field. Jahmyr Gibbs was stuffed for a two-yard loss, handing Green Bay possession deep in Lions territory with less than five minutes remaining. Oct 25, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Detroit Lions head coach Dan Campbell looks on during the second quarter against the Green Bay Packers at Ford Field. Mandatory Credit: Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Dan Campbell Explains His Risky Fourth-Down Decision Following the victory, Campbell was asked why he decided to take such an enormous gamble with the game hanging in the balance. His explanation was simple, and it reflected the confidence he had in both his offense and defense. “I thought we would get it,” Campbell said following Detroit’s win. “Two, I thought we would get the ball back if it didn’t work out.” DC on the decision to go for it on fourth down deep in Lions territory pic.twitter.com/pk1moEZiQa — Detroit Lions (@Lions) October 26, 2026 The decision was especially surprising considering how well Detroit’s defense had performed against Jordan Love and the Packers offense. Green Bay managed just 60 rushing yards, and the Lions had already forced several important stops throughout the game. Campbell’s confidence in his defense ultimately proved justified, although the Packers came dangerously close to taking the lead. After taking over in Detroit territory, Green Bay moved into position for a 35-yard field goal, but D.J. Wonnum got a hand on Trey Smack’s attempt to keep the game tied. Lions Defense Bails Out Campbell The failed fourth-down conversion could have been the defining moment of Detroit’s afternoon, but the defense refused to let it happen. Green Bay’s missed opportunity gave Jared Goff and the Lions offense another possession, and this time they delivered when it mattered most. Goff guided Detroit down the field before Jake Bates connected on a 22-yard field goal as time expired. The victory improved the Lions to 4-2 while dropping the Packers to 4-3, giving Detroit an important win over its division rival. Detroit finished with 415 total yards, including 303 passing yards and two touchdowns from Goff. As we previously reported , Jameson Williams delivered a spectacular opening-drive touchdown and finished the game with five receptions for 91 yards and two scores. The Lions also received a huge performance from Amon-Ra St. Brown , who caught nine passes for 153 yards. Meanwhile, Gibbs rushed for 11

With the game tied late in the fourth quarter, Campbell elected to go for it on fourth-and-1 from Detroit’s own 22-yard line, a decision that immediately backfired. Rather than punt the football and trust a defense that had played exceptionally well throughout the afternoon, Campbell kept his offense on the field. Jahmyr Gibbs was stuffed for a two-yard loss, handing Green Bay possession deep in Lions territory with less than five minutes remaining. Oct 25, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Detroit Lions head coach Dan Campbell looks on during the second quarter against the Green Bay Packers at Ford Field. Mandatory Credit: Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Dan Campbell Explains His Risky Fourth-Down Decision Following the victory, Campbell was asked why he decided to take such an enormous gamble with the game hanging in the balance. His explanation was simple, and it reflected the confidence he had in both his offense and defense. “I thought we would get it,” Campbell said following Detroit’s win. “Two, I thought we would get the ball back if it didn’t work out.” DC on the decision to go for it on fourth down deep in Lions territory pic.twitter.com/pk1moEZiQa — Detroit Lions (@Lions) October 26, 2026 The decision was especially surprising considering how well Detroit’s defense had performed against Jordan Love and the Packers offense. Green Bay managed just 60 rushing yards, and the Lions had already forced several important stops throughout the game. Campbell’s confidence in his defense ultimately proved justified, although the Packers came dangerously close to taking the lead. After taking over in Detroit territory, Green Bay moved into position for a 35-yard field goal, but D.J. Wonnum got a hand on Trey Smack’s attempt to keep the game tied. Lions Defense Bails Out Campbell The failed fourth-down conversion could have been the defining moment of Detroit’s afternoon, but the defense refused to let it happen. Green Bay’s missed opportunity gave Jared Goff and the Lions offense another possession, and this time they delivered when it mattered most. Goff guided Detroit down the field before Jake Bates connected on a 22-yard field goal as time expired. The victory improved the Lions to 4-2 while dropping the Packers to 4-3, giving Detroit an important win over its division rival. Detroit finished with 415 total yards, including 303 passing yards and two touchdowns from Goff. As we previously reported , Jameson Williams delivered a spectacular opening-drive touchdown and finished the game with five receptions for 91 yards and two scores. The Lions also received a huge performance from Amon-Ra St. Brown , who caught nine passes for 153 yards. Meanwhile, Gibbs rushed for 116 yards on 29 carries despite being stopped on the crucial fourth-down attempt. Campbell’s Aggressiveness Remains a Double-Edged Sword Campbell has never been afraid to gamble on fourth down, and that mentality has become part of Detroit’s identity during his tenure. However, going for it deep in his own territory with the score tied and less than five minutes remaining was the kind of decision that could have overshadowed everything the Lions accomplished Sunday. Detroit finished 0-for-2 on fourth-down attempts while Green Bay converted three of its four opportunities. The Lions nevertheless found a way to survive, thanks largely to a defense that limited the Packers to 324 total yards and came through when Campbell needed it most. The final result was another reminder that Campbell’s aggressive approach can create both tremendous opportunities and unnecessary risks. This time, the Lions had enough defense, resilience, and a little good fortune to make sure his most controversial decision didn’t cost them the game.

item.title: Video Shows SEC Player in Apparent Altercation as South Carolina Fans Flood the Field
item.description: An unforgettable SEC clash ended in total postgame pandemonium at Williams-Brice Stadium after a dramatic 27–24 upset by South Carolina over No. 11 Tennessee instantly transformed into a chaotic, headline-grabbing scene on the field. As thousands of overjoyed Gamecock supporters swarmed the playing surface in the immediate aftermath of a walk-off field goal, the sudden influx created bottlenecked exits and safety risks for the visiting team. Chaos erupted after Gamecocks’ upset South Carolina secured a dramatic 27–24 upset victory over No. 11 Tennessee at Williams-Brice Stadium, clinched by kicker Malik Orsan’s walk-off 48-yard field goal. As the ball split the uprights, thousands of Gamecock supporters immediately poured over the walls and swarmed the playing surface to celebrate the signature conference win. South Carolina fans jump the hedges as they storm the field after a college football game between Tennessee and South Carolina at Williams-Brice Stadium in Columbia, S.C., on Oct. 24, 2026. As Tennessee personnel navigated the postgame congestion, video clips circulated on social media highlighting two distinct physical altercations involving Volunteers players. A seven-second video clip captured an individual holding a mobile device or camera close to the exiting Tennessee players while waving directly in their faces. As the crowd moved around the team, senior defensive lineman Daevin Hobbs was captured walking through the frame carrying a small rod or object in his left hand. Hobbs lowered his right shoulder into the spectator, knocking the fan flat onto the turf before continuing toward the locker room tunnel. A secondary video clip filmed near the field exit pathway captured a physical exchange between opposing players. Senior linebacker Jeremiah Telander was filmed advancing through the crowd toward South Carolina freshman defensive back Triston Lewis . Telander threw a right-handed swing aimed at Lewis. The postgame chaos also drew renewed attention to SEC field-storming regulations, with the conference facing heavy standard fines for the massive influx of spectators onto the playing field. South Carolina will be fined The primary party facing financial penalties is the University of South Carolina. South Carolina allowed thousands of fans to breach security barriers and storm the playing surface at Williams-Brice Stadium immediately following Malik Orsan’s walk-off 48-yard field goal. Under Southeastern Conference access-to-competition-area policy, any unauthorized field or court rush results in a flat $500,000 fine. The fine is paid directly to the opposing institution, the University of Tennessee. While the university itself bears the administrative fine for the field rush, individual disciplinary actions and potential league penalties could follow the physical altercations caught on camera. The SEC office and Tennessee athletic administration review postgame tape following physical incidents involving fans or opposing players. Dep

item.title: NFL Week 7: Biggest Winners and Losers, Including Cam Skattebo and the Falcons
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect With 11 games between the morning, early, and late-afternoon windows of NFL Week 7, Sunday delivered another action-packed event for football fans. Some players and teams took major steps ahead on Sunday. Others took steps backward. Through it all, many clear winners and losers stood out. Below is a compilation of the best and worst from NFL Sunday in Week 7. Related: 5 Jonathan Taylor Trade Destinations That Make Sense Before NFL Deadline Loser: New Orleans Saints Rushing Attack Oct 25, 2026; Paris, FRA; Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Jalen Ramsey (5) makes a tackle on New Orleans Saints running back Alvin Kamara (41) during the second quarter at Stade de France. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images The New Orleans Saints didn’t trade Alvin Kamara this offseason, preferring to keep the five-time Pro Bowler instead of getting some late-round draft compensation in return. Yet, Kamara hasn’t been effective. That continued on Sunday in Paris, when the 31-year-old saw just six carries but took them for five yards. He was much better as a pass-catcher in open space, catching seven passes for 57 yards. But again, the Saints’ rushing attack finished with a paltry 18 yards on 17 attempts. Related: 5 NFL Trades That Could Happen Before Nov. 10 Deadline Winner: Atlanta Falcons Oct 25, 2026; Atlanta, Georgia, USA; Atlanta Falcons wide receiver Drake London (5) celebrates with teammates after catching a 21-yard touchdown pass against the San Francisco 49ers at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images On a day when half of their division lost, the Atlanta Falcons are big winners for being the first team to take down the San Francisco 49ers. Not only did it bring them a half-game within the division lead, the Falcons proved that they can beat one of the very best teams in the NFL. While Michael Penix Jr. was good again, the Defense played a huge role, forcing two fumbles and intercepting Brock Purdy twice. It may not have been their biggest victory in the point margin, this was the Falcons’ best win of the 2026 season, so far. Loser: Carolina Panthers Rush Defense Oct 25, 2026; Charlotte, North Carolina, USA; Tampa Bay Buccaneers running back Bucky Irving (7) celebrates after scoring a touchdown against the Carolina Panthers during the first half at Bank of America Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jim Dedmon-Imagn Images The Carolina Panthers’ defense has taken a considerable step back this season after ranking 15th in points allowed in 2025. They allowed a season-high 43 on Sunday. It’s not an outcome anyone in Carolina expected, especially when they allowed just 63 passing yards, mainly because Tampa Bay averaged half a first down every time they ran the ball (5.3 YPC). Now falling to 3-3, Carolina’s defense made them big-time losers on Sunday. Related: 4 Vita Vea Trade Destinations Ahead of NFL Trade Deadline Winner: Deshaun Watson Oct 25, 2026; Nashville, Tennessee, USA; Cleveland Browns quarterback D

Related: 5 Josh Sweat Trade Destinations After NFL Rumors Heat Up Loser: Trey Smack Green Bay Packers kicker Trey Smack (28) attempts a field goal against Detroit Lions during the first half at Ford Field in Detroit on Sunday, Oct. 25, 2026. While the Green Bay Packers’ rushing attack once again did the team no favors, neither did kicker Trey Smack, who made just one of three field goal attempts. That includes a 26-yard attempt that went wide right in the first quarter. Related: 5 Tyreek Hill Landing Spots As NFL Rumors Heat Up Winner: J.J. McCarthy and Cam Skattebo Oct 25, 2026; Houston, Texas, USA; New York Giants quarterback J.J. Mandatory Credit: Troy Taormina-Imagn Images The New York Giants may have both discovered their winning formula and found their franchise quarterback/running back of the future in the same game. J.J. McCarthy continues to not only look downfield, he’s making opponents pay, connecting on two 40+ yard passing plays. Overall, he completed 20 of 28 passes for 250 yards. While he did take three sacks, McCarthy didn’t commit any turnovers. As for Cam Skattebo, he busted his way out of the doghouse by going off for 124 yards and a touchdown on just 17 attempts. Yet, his best play was a 42-yard game-sealing rush that set up a 30-yard Devin Singletary touchdown a play later. Related: 5 Minnesota Vikings Trades To Capitalize on Hot Start Winner: Bo Nix Oct 25, 2026; Glendale, Arizona, USA; Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix (10) runs to score a touchdown against the Arizona Cardinals during the first half at State Farm Stadium. Nix still didn’t complete many of his passes, just 15-of-29, but he ended up racking up 222 yards and a touchdown in the process. Impressively, he also led the Broncos with 74 rushing yards and a touchdown thanks to a 62-yard scamper with a wide-open rushing lane. This was one of Nix’s beter starts of the season, but can he keep it up? Related: 6 Khalil Mack Trade Destinations As NFL Rumors Heat Up

item.title: 49ers’ Brock Purdy explains brutal blunder that cost San Francisco during Falcons upset
item.description: Credit: Brett Davis-Imagn Images 49ers’ Brock Purdy explains brutal blunder that cost San Francisco during Falcons upset appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Coach Kyle Shanahan, QB Brock Purdy and other familiar faces led the 49ers into gridiron battle against the Atlanta Falcons in Week 7 action that included a Christian McCaffrey injury scare . Fans debated whether San Francisco could finish the season undefeated like the 1972 Miami Dolphins ahead of the game and got their answer as Atlanta won 29-20 during a day when Purdy was intercepted twice. One interception came when Jessie Bates dove near the sideline and snagged Purdy’s pass, which fans thought he intended to throw out-of-bounds. Purdy explained after the game that he was trying to find a 49ers receiver who wasn’t where he placed it. “Yeah, I thought maybe Christian Kirk on the scramble was gonna be there, but towards the end of the throw, as I was going to throw I was like, no it’s not, and sort of went to just throw it away by the sideline, and then Bates all of a sudden came across and made a play, and I was like, you gotta be kidding me. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “So in that moment, man, I gotta completely throw the ball away if I’m not gonna make an attempt to a receiver, so,” Purdy added. The day began with news of the 49ers’ potential trade interest in Colts defensive tackle DeForest Buckner , who once played in San Francisco. The 49ers’ defense held Bijan Robinson, the Falcons’ star running back, to just 63 yards on the day while QB Michael Penix Jr. had 213 yards and made them count with three passing touchdowns. Now 6-1, Shanahan, Purdy and the rest of the 49ers are scheduled to face the Raiders at home on November 8 after a bye week, giving them time to recoup and reassess for what figures to be a grueling midseason run. item.title: Kyler Murray Sends Clear Message After Leading Vikings Past Colts
item.description: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - OCTOBER 25: Kyler Murray #1 of the Minnesota Vikings warms up against the Indianapolis Colts before the game at U.S. Bank Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images) Getty The Minnesota Vikings needed a spark from Kyler Murray on Sunday. They got one with his legs. Murray’s 35-yard scramble helped set up the Vikings’ only touchdown in a 16-10 victory over the Indianapolis Colts on October 25, keeping Minnesota undefeated at 6-0. But after delivering one of the biggest plays of the afternoon, Murray made it clear that he isn’t necessarily looking to become a more frequent runner. Asked after the game whether he was eager to find more opportunities to take off, Murray pushed back on the suggestion. “No. I wouldn’t say that. I wouldn’t say that at all,” Murray said. “If coach calls my number, I’m ready for it. If the play presents itself to allow me to do what I did on the run, then that’s what it is. But I’m not … I wouldn’t say I’m eager.” It’s an interesting position for a quarterback whose mobility has helped an otherwise inconsistent Vikings offense remain undefeated. LIVE: QB Kyler Murray https://t.co/xQWhSmWxzn — Minnesota Vikings (@Vikings) October 25, 2026 Kyler Murray Explains His Approach to Running With the Vikings Murray’s biggest play came early in the fourth quarter, with Minnesota trailing 10-6. Facing a third down, Murray escaped Indianapolis’ pressure and sprinted 35 yards before being brought down near the goal line. On the following play, he connected with tight end T.J. Hockenson for a five-yard touchdown that gave Minnesota its first lead. According to the Minnesota Star Tribune , it was the longest run by a Vikings quarterback since Joe Webb’s 65-yard touchdown against Detroit in 2011. Murray explained that the Colts were playing man coverage and an opening developed when pressure arrived. “At that point I saw an opening,” Murray said. “Got to get out there and just make a play. That’s all I was trying to do.” Still, the former No. 1 overall pick emphasized that he prefers operating from the pocket rather than actively looking for rushing opportunities. “I’m always trying to stay in the pocket and make a play, throw from the pocket,” Murray said. “But if that happens, that happens.” He also acknowledged how much pressure his mobility can place on opposing defenses, particularly when plays break down and Minnesota’s receivers have time to get open. That philosophy is consistent with head coach Kevin O’Connell’s previous comments about Murray’s athleticism. Following Minnesota’s October 11 win over New Orleans, O’Connell explained that the team wanted to take advantage of Murray’s mobility without prescribing exactly when he should run. Against Indianapolis, that flexibility produced the Vikings’ most important offensive sequence. (Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images) Getty The Minnesota Vikings needed a spark from Kyler Murray on Sunday. They got one with his legs. Murray’s 35-yard scramble helped set up the Vikings’ only touchdown in a 16-10 victory over the Indianapolis Colts on October 25, keeping Minnesota undefeated at 6-0. But after delivering one of the biggest plays of the afternoon, Murray made it clear that he isn’t necessarily looking to become a more frequent runner. Asked after the game whether he was eager to find more opportunities to take off, Murray pushed back on the suggestion. “No. I wouldn’t say that. I wouldn’t say that at all,” Murray said. “If coach calls my number, I’m ready for it. If the play presents itself to allow me to do what I did on the run, then that’s what it is. But I’m not … I wouldn’t say I’m eager.” It’s an interesting position for a quarterback whose mobility has helped an otherwise inconsistent Vikings offense remain undefeated. LIVE: QB Kyler Murray https://t.co/xQWhSmWxzn — Minnesota Vikings (@Vikings) October 25, 2026 Kyler Murray Explains His Approach to Running With the Vikings Murray’s biggest play came early in the fourth quarter, with Minnesota trailing 10-6. Facing a third down, Murray escaped Indianapolis’ pressure and sprinted 35 yards before being brought down near the goal line. On the following play, he connected with tight end T.J. Hockenson for a five-yard touchdown that gave Minnesota its first lead. According to the Minnesota Star Tribune , it was the longest run by a Vikings quarterback since Joe Webb’s 65-yard touchdown against Detroit in 2011. Murray explained that the Colts were playing man coverage and an opening developed when pressure arrived. “At that point I saw an opening,” Murray said. “Got to get out there and just make a play. That’s all I was trying to do.” Still, the former No. 1 overall pick emphasized that he prefers operating from the pocket rather than actively looking for rushing opportunities. “I’m always trying to stay in the pocket and make a play, throw from the pocket,” Murray said. “But if that happens, that happens.” He also acknowledged how much pressure his mobility can place on opposing defenses, particularly when plays break down and Minnesota’s receivers have time to get open. That philosophy is consistent with head coach Kevin O’Connell’s previous comments about Murray’s athleticism. Following Minnesota’s October 11 win over New Orleans, O’Connell explained that the team wanted to take advantage of Murray’s mobility without prescribing exactly when he should run. Against Indianapolis, that flexibility produced the Vikings’ most important offensive sequence. Kyler Murray Acknowledges Vikings’ Offensive Struggles Despite the victory, Minnesota’s offense had another difficult afternoon. Murray completed 14 of 24 passes for 150 yards and one touchdown. Justin Jefferson finished with four receptions for 44 yards, while the Vikings managed just one touchdown across the entire game. Minnesota also converted only three of 11 third-down opportunities and scored a touchdown on one of its two red-zone possessions. Afterward, Murray expressed confidence in the offense but acknowledged its inability to finish drives. “We got to put the ball in the end zone,” Murray said. “At the end of the day, that’s what it comes down to.” Murray agreed with O’Connell’s assessment that the offense was getting closer to reaching its potential. “My confidence will never waver in the group that we have,” he said. For now, the defense continues to provide Minnesota with a substantial margin for error. The Vikings held Indianapolis scoreless in the second half, and Harrison Smith intercepted Daniel Jones late in the fourth quarter to secure the victory. Murray wasn’t surprised. “Nothing that they do surprises me,” he said of Minnesota’s defense. “It’s a really special group over there.” Minnesota will face a tougher test of its offensive progress in Week 8 against the Detroit Lions . The Vikings have continued finding ways to win, but Sunday’s performance offered another reminder that Murray and the offense still have work ahead. item.title: What Angel City’s playoff qualification means to fans and players
item.description: Angel City FC forward Sveindís Jónsdóttir (32) raises her arms after Angel City's second goal of the match during an NWSL soccer game against Bay FC, Saturday, October 24, 2026 in Los Angeles. LOS ANGELES – For the second time in club history, Angel City Football Club will play in the 2026 National Women’s Soccer League playoffs, and the ACFC community is ready. “I am so excited. I hope if they get to the top four, we'll hopefully come and see them play and I'll bring her [younger sister Alani] along. I'm excited to see them play in the playoffs," said Jeanine, a young Angel City fan. The sisters have supported ACFC with their family for two years and have supported their favorite player, Gisele Thompson. The Portland Thorns’ week 25 win over the North Carolina Courage clinched playoff spots for Angel City and three other teams. ACFC last reached the postseason in 2023, during its second season in the league, but was eliminated in its first match following a 1-nil loss to the Seattle Reign. At the time, only the top six teams reached the postseason. Beginning with the 2024 season, the league expanded, and the top eight teams now qualify for the single-elimination format. Angel City joined the NWSL as an expansion side five seasons ago, debuting in 2022 and giving Los Angeles its first professional women’s soccer team since the Los Angeles Sol played its lone 2009 season in the now-defunct Women’s Professional Soccer league. The club’s reach extends far beyond Southern California. “It’s very inspirational. We don’t have a team in Fresno, so [Angel City] is the closest thing, and we absolutely love it. We’re so excited [for playoffs]. We’ve been in it, and we just want them to win—the culture, the community, the players. I just love it. I’m over the moon,” said Angel City fan Shannon, who’s followed the club with friends since its inaugural season. She traveled nearly four hours from Fresno to Los Angeles to see Angel City’s 2-0 win over Bay FC in its second-to-last home game of the season on Saturday. A NEW ERA FOR ANGEL CITY For team captain Sarah Gorden, this season’s team is different than that 2023 squad. “This team is different than any other Angel City team I've ever been on. Obviously, you're seeing that with the results and the momentum,” she told The Sporting Tribune. “Our team is really different than any other team…We're calm…We do what needs to be done to win games. Whatever happens in the middle, we'll do what we have to do to win the game. So we're extremely effective, and that's what you need going into the playoffs. So I'm really excited to see how we do.” Gorden signed with the team in 2021 and is one of four inaugural season players still with the team. During Saturday’s press conference, she acknowledged fans' commitment and their journey with the team. “It’s easy to play for them [fans] because they’ve sacrificed so much for us,” said Gorden. The sisters have supported ACFC with their family for two years and have supported their favorite player, Gisele Thompson. Angel City joined the NWSL as an expansion side five seasons ago, debuting in 2022 and giving Los Angeles its first professional women’s soccer team since the Los Angeles Sol played its lone 2009 season in the now-defunct Women’s Professional Soccer league. The club’s reach extends far beyond Southern California. “It’s very inspirational. We don’t have a team in Fresno, so [Angel City] is the closest thing, and we absolutely love it. I’m over the moon,” said Angel City fan Shannon, who’s followed the club with friends since its inaugural season. She traveled nearly four hours from Fresno to Los Angeles to see Angel City’s 2-0 win over Bay FC in its second-to-last home game of the season on Saturday. A NEW ERA FOR ANGEL CITY For team captain Sarah Gorden, this season’s team is different than that 2023 squad. “This team is different than any other Angel City team I've ever been on. Obviously, you're seeing that with the results and the momentum,” she told The Sporting Tribune. “Our team is really different than any other team…We're calm…We do what needs to be done to win games. Whatever happens in the middle, we'll do what we have to do to win the game. So we're extremely effective, and that's what you need going into the playoffs. So I'm really excited to see how we do.” Gorden signed with the team in 2021 and is one of four inaugural season players still with the team. During Saturday’s press conference, she acknowledged fans' commitment and their journey with the team. “It’s easy to play for them [fans] because they’ve sacrificed so much for us,” said Gorden. Angel City FC fans celebrate after the team scored a second goal during an NWSL soccer game against Bay FC, Saturday, October 24, 2026 in Los Angeles. Edwin So - The Sporting Tribune Angel City FC fans celebrate after the team scored a second goal during an NWSL soccer game against Bay FC, Saturday, October 24, 2026 in Los Angeles. Saturday’s match comes at the tail end of arguably one of Angel City’s best runs in club history. It marks the ninth consecutive match in which Angel City remained unbeaten. After a remarkable turnaround in the final third of the season, Angel City (14-7-8, 49 pts.) entered match week 26 in fifth on the league table. The club’s 2026 campaign has featured four new club records. Maiara Niehues and Sveindís Jónsdóttir lead the team in scoring with nine goals each- the most scored by an Angel City player in a single regular season. Goalkeeper Angelina Anderson has set a personal best and club single-season record with ten shutouts so far. The young talent has also had breakout runs. Rookie Taylor Suarez made league history, scoring just 21 seconds after entering the match to set the NWSL record for the fastest goal by an in-game substitute when the team faced Seattle Reign FC on September 15 , and she earned her fourth goal in a five-match span against Denver. Defender Evelyn Shores set the season-high with eight assists. “We are very proud of the players and all of our staff for reaching this milestone. We are in a good run of form at a great time, and this team is hungry for more,” said ACFC Sporting Director Mark Parsons in a press release announcing the team's playoff push . “We can't wait to keep this going for our fans and for the city of LA." The win over Bay FC highlighted the club’s mentality to finish the season strong. “We just made sure to do our best to really focus on this game; the job's not finished yet. We really want to go into the playoffs with a lot of good momentum from having really good performance in these last two games of the regular season,” said Anderson. The final match of the 2026 regular season will take place at Dignity Health Sports Park in Carson, home of MLS’ LA Galaxy, on November 1st at 2 PM PST. Angel City will host a “Celebración de Culturas” as it takes on the Boston Legacy.

item.title: Max Verstappen jokes Red Bull should abandon radios after United States GP struggles
item.description: Motorsport photo Max Verstappen has complained about Red Bull's repeated radio issues, calling them "a disaster" and joking that they should start communicating in sign language instead. The four-time champion finished third behind winner Kimi Antonelli and Charles Leclerc at the United States Grand Prix after what was a frustrating and issue-ridden race. And to make things even more difficult, the Dutchman suffered radio issues that made communication with the pitwall much harder than it should have been. Asked in the press conference following the race how frustrating it is to have those types of issues for a second time, Verstappen was keen to correct the journalist. “It’s not the second time. It’s already, I don’t know how many times this year. Maybe we should just start communicating in sign language. It’s probably cheaper as well. It’s a disaster. Yeah, it’s a disaster. It’s really frustrating, to be honest,” he said. Verstappen was not the only Red Bull driver to be affected. Team-mate Isack Hadjar , who finished sixth after dropping from third on the opening lap, said he could not hear his engineers properly and left the pits with the wrong engine setting potentially as a result. “And then I have poor radio coverage. I can’t hear what’s happening in the pits. I leave the pits with the wrong map,” Hadjar told Sky Sports F1. Radio was only one of several problems Verstappen listed after the race. He was disappointed with the team’s tyre choices, lamented a slow pitstop and highlighted inconsistent behaviour from the power unit, which he said had made it impossible to build a rhythm. Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing “Too many issues with the power unit, where it was just very inconsistent behaviour around the corners, every lap, every corner, different behaviour. So, you can’t build up a rhythm, you can’t build any kind of consistency in the car. I had a slow pitstop. So, yeah, too many things today that just didn’t go well.” The result ended a run of two consecutive wins for the Red Bull driver, who had won in Sepang and Singapore, and he admitted he had been fortunate to finish on the podium. “We still managed to get on the podium, maybe a little bit lucky with the VSC at the end, but I’ll take it,” he said. It was Verstappen’s 10th podium of the season. But with five rounds remaining, he is now totally out of contention for the title. If Mercedes' Antonelli finishes in the top nine in Mexico next weekend, he will be the 2026 Formula 1 world champion. Red Bull arrived in Austin fighting McLaren for third in the constructors’ championship, and Verstappen admitted the team had fallen below its usual standards. “Normally we’re very good at these things, but today we weren’t,” he ended. item.title: 49ers Called Out for Losing ‘$40 Million Per Year’ Edge Rusher
item.description: New Orleans Saints edge rusher Chase Young. Getty In 2026, we’re finally seeing the player the Washington Commanders thought they drafted with the No. 2 overall pick in the 2020 NFL Draft While Chase Young is doing it two teams later with the New Orleans Saints, he’s doing it at such a high level that he’s now second in the NFL with 7.0 sacks through 7 games, following a dominant performance in his team’s loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers in Paris. Young trails Houston Texans edge rusher and NFL All-Pro Will Anderson Jr. by just a half-sack. For a team that struggles to get to the passer, it’s likely a bitter pill to swallow for the Commanders and their fans, who cut bait on Young with a trade to the San Francisco 49ers midway through the 2023 season. It’s also a bitter pill for the 49ers and their fans to swallow as they could have had Young for a relatively paltry sum before the 2024 season. “Chase Young has 22.5 sacks since leaving the 49ers after the 2023 season,” The Associated Press wrote on X . “No one on Niners has more than 11 in that span.” “Chase Young is having a terrific season in New Orleans,” The Athletic’s David Aldridge wrote on his official X account on Sunday. “Didn’t work out in D.C., obviously, but he’s resurrected his career with the Saints. Good for him.” “Saints don’t play many island games, so if you’re just watching them for the first time … this is how Chase Young has been playing for the last two seasons,” Saints reporter Nick Underhill wrote on X . “He’s about to be a $40+ million/year man.” Chase Young gets the take down on third down! PITvsNO on NFL NetworkStream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/ziEuwDpY7C — NFL (@NFL) October 25, 2026 Chase Young Headed for Massive New Contract Headed into his 8th season and now with the New Orleans Saints — his 3rd team — Bleacher Report’s Gary Davenport called Young’s next big-money deal 1 of the NFL’s “Most Important Contract Decisions” in 2026. Young signed a 3-year, $51 million contract with the Saints in March 2025. “Last year, it finally came together for Saints edge-rusher Chase Young,” Davenport wrote on August 2. “It didn’t look like it was going to — the former No. 2 overall pick missed the season’s first five games with a calf injury. But once Young was back on the field, he caught fire—a career-high 10 sacks in 12 games … Young is under contract through 2027 at a bargain price relative to what other high-end edge-rushers make. If he can back up last year’s numbers with a hot start in 2026, extending the 27-year-old now could save the Saints a boatload of scratch down the road.” Chase Young Part of Dreadful Run of Draft Picks After securing the first big-time payday of his career, Young delivered his best season in 2025 as the Saints were 1 of the NFL’s most-improved teams down the stretch under rookie head coach Kellen Moore . Young’s deal was being singled out as one of the NFL’s “Best Free Agent Signings” of the 2025 cycle by PFF’s Bradley Locker . It’s a far cry from when
item.content:encoded: New Orleans Saints edge rusher Chase Young. Getty In 2026, we’re finally seeing the player the Washington Commanders thought they drafted with the No. 2 overall pick in the 2020 NFL Draft While Chase Young is doing it two teams later with the New Orleans Saints, he’s doing it at such a high level that he’s now second in the NFL with 7.0 sacks through 7 games, following a dominant performance in his team’s loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers in Paris. Young trails Houston Texans edge rusher and NFL All-Pro Will Anderson Jr. by just a half-sack. For a team that struggles to get to the passer, it’s likely a bitter pill to swallow for the Commanders and their fans, who cut bait on Young with a trade to the San Francisco 49ers midway through the 2023 season. It’s also a bitter pill for the 49ers and their fans to swallow as they could have had Young for a relatively paltry sum before the 2024 season. “Chase Young has 22.5 sacks since leaving the 49ers after the 2023 season,” The Associated Press wrote on X . “No one on Niners has more than 11 in that span.” “Chase Young is having a terrific season in New Orleans,” The Athletic’s David Aldridge wrote on his official X account on Sunday. “Didn’t work out in D.C., obviously, but he’s resurrected his career with the Saints. Good for him.” “Saints don’t play many island games, so if you’re just watching them for the first time … this is how Chase Young has been playing for the last two seasons,” Saints reporter Nick Underhill wrote on X . “He’s about to be a $40+ million/year man.” Chase Young gets the take down on third down! PITvsNO on NFL NetworkStream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/ziEuwDpY7C — NFL (@NFL) October 25, 2026 Chase Young Headed for Massive New Contract Headed into his 8th season and now with the New Orleans Saints — his 3rd team — Bleacher Report’s Gary Davenport called Young’s next big-money deal 1 of the NFL’s “Most Important Contract Decisions” in 2026. Young signed a 3-year, $51 million contract with the Saints in March 2025. “Last year, it finally came together for Saints edge-rusher Chase Young,” Davenport wrote on August 2. “It didn’t look like it was going to — the former No. 2 overall pick missed the season’s first five games with a calf injury. But once Young was back on the field, he caught fire—a career-high 10 sacks in 12 games … Young is under contract through 2027 at a bargain price relative to what other high-end edge-rushers make. If he can back up last year’s numbers with a hot start in 2026, extending the 27-year-old now could save the Saints a boatload of scratch down the road.” Chase Young Part of Dreadful Run of Draft Picks After securing the first big-time payday of his career, Young delivered his best season in 2025 as the Saints were 1 of the NFL’s most-improved teams down the stretch under rookie head coach Kellen Moore . Young’s deal was being singled out as one of the NFL’s “Best Free Agent Signings” of the 2025 cycle by PFF’s Bradley Locker . It’s a far cry from when Young’s time with the Commanders ended midway through the 2023 season as one of the biggest busts in franchise history. “The Saints made a rarely large move when they retained Young on a three-year, $51 million contract to prevent him from leaving,” Locker wrote. “In turn, Young absolutely dominated when on the field with an 86.3 PFF pass-rush grade and a 15.2% pass-rush win rate. The former No. 2 overall pick appears to have settled into form with the Saints.” Young was part of an incredible run of 1st-round picks who didn’t pan out for the Commanders — 6 picks in 5 years from 2019 to 2023 no longer on their roster by the end of the 2024 season. The biggest bust of the bunch was Young. Following a torn ACL suffered in Week 10 of the 2021 regular season, Young missed 22 of the next 25 regular-season games, including all but 3 games in 2022 — a 2-season stretch in which he had just 1.5 sacks. Young revamped his career in 2023 with 7.5 sacks while playing for both the Commanders and the San Francisco 49ers after a midseason trade and was a role player as the 49ers made it to the Super Bowl. Young took the momentum from his time with the 49ers and parlayed that into a 1-year, $13 million contract with the Saints in 2024, when he played in every regular-season game for the first time in his career and finished with 5.5 sacks, 8 TFL and 21 QB hits. item.title: Charles Leclerc reveals Ferrari breakthrough after United States GP podium
item.description: Motorsport photo Charles Leclerc believes he has "unlocked something" in his driving with Ferrari in recent races and is confident he will have a shot at victory before the end of the 2026 Formula 1 season. The Monegasque driver finished second in the United States Grand Prix, 13 seconds behind race winner and championship leader Kimi Antonelli, after battling Max Verstappen and Lando Norris . It followed another second-place in Singapore, and Leclerc said his feeling with the car had improved over the last few race weekends. "Whether I can convert that into a win is a bit difficult to predict, because it's such fine margins, and it also depends on what the upgrade plans of the others are in upcoming races," Leclerc explained during the post-race press conference. "But the feeling with the car is getting better and better. These cars are very specific and unique, and I feel like, over the last two or three races, I've unlocked something again in terms of driving, and particularly the set-up with my driving. Charles Leclerc, Ferrari Charles Leclerc, Ferrari "Just both together, we've taken a step forward, and I just feel much more comfortable with the car. So I hope that this will result in a win soon. Whether it's in Singapore or here in Austin, we were quite close, so I'm confident that we'll have a shot at winning a race before the end of the season." The United States Grand Prix kicked off the penultimate triple-header of the season, and the teams and drivers will now head to Mexico City for the Mexican Grand Prix next weekend. With five race weekends remaining, assuming the final two races in Qatar and Abu Dhabi go ahead as planned, Leclerc sits fifth in the drivers' standings but is still in the fight for second. Mercedes' George Russell currently sits second with 242 points. Lewis Hamilton , Max Verstappen and Leclerc are third, fourth and fifth respectively, with only nine points separating second and fifth. To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

item.title: Mbappé double secures Real Madrid late victory at Barcelona after Raphinha leveller
item.description: Thirteen years later, José Mourinho led Real Madrid into the Camp Nou as one team and them out again as another having secured the kind of late victory he loves and which opens up a whole new world. With just three minutes and the final reserves of energy remaining, a wonderful moment of skill from Jude Bellingham found Eduardo Camavinga and set them on one last run. Camavinga sprinted free, skilfully slipped Pau Cubarsí and pulled back for Kylian Mbappé to provide the finish, a little bit of history written. “The world that loves football will have stopped to watch this and they won’t have gone disappointed; this was two teams that played to win,” Mourinho said. It had been an intense, breathless ride, a proper battle, and it was his team who won it. Arriving right on time, Mbappé scored his second to make it 2-1, the Camp Nou falling quiet and their team given no time to react. They had drawn level after Mbappé’s opener, Raphinha scoring, but could not do it again. Continue reading...

item.title: Fernandes gamble leaves Carrick to carry the can for United’s institutional failures | Will Unwin
item.description: Leaving out his captain was doomed to fail but so are the club under the current leadership and the fans at Old Trafford know that all too well Dropping your captain, who has held the team together for most of the past five years, is a bold move from a man whose job is on the line. It was very much a make-or-break decision from Michael Carrick to leave out Bruno Fernandes against Bournemouth. It did not work and Carrick knew the consequences if it failed and will probably pay the price for it, but he should not be alone. Carrick said the decision to drop the Portuguese playmaker was purely based on football reasons but criticising his manager after the desperate defeat to Como cannot have helped. Clearly Carrick disagreed with his captain’s comments on the lack of pressing in the Champions League fixture. It was somewhat telling that Lisandro Martínez kept his place despite pointing out the director of football, Jason Wilcox, was a hindrance to the club the previous week. Continue reading...

After another Europa League setback at home to Celta Vigo on Thursday, the champions bounced back with a victory that restored their four-point cushion over Rangers at the top. The home side, who are bottom, took an early lead through Owen Elding but it was swiftly cancelled out by a Jason Kerr own goal before Duran’s 10th of the season edged the visitors ahead just before the break. item.title: Isak applies finishing touch as Liverpool bring Brighton’s winning run to an end
item.description: Brighton’s impressive run was blown off course at Anfield where Liverpool performed with an appetite and urgency at both ends of the pitch that showed Andoni Iraola’s methods taking root. It was Liverpool, deserving winners on home soil for the first time in the Premier League this season, who looked upwardly mobile. There was more evidence of the expensive trio of Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Bradley Barcola feeling at home and adapting to Iraola’s demands. Wirtz was instrumental in an opening goal officially credited to Brighton’s Pascal Gross and Isak scored for the sixth time in six Premier League appearances to shatter the visitors’ sequence of four successive league wins. The sight of Barcola sprinting back to help his defence and Ronald Araújo smashing into challenges, as Liverpool stubbornly defended their lead and their box in the second half, satisfied Iraola just as much as his side’s incisiveness before the break. Continue reading...

item.title: Ballon d’Or ceremony returns to England in nod to ‘revolutionary’ Stanley Matthews
item.description: Matthews’ family ‘very excited’ as London Palladium hosts event 70 years after first award at Blackpool town hall When football’s dignitaries assemble on Monday at the London Palladium for the Ballon d’Or ceremony it will be a far cry from the first awards 70 years ago. That was held in the slightly less glamorous surroundings of Blackpool town hall, where Stanley Matthews was presented with the prize by Gabriel Hanot, the visionary editor of L’Équipe who came up with the idea of crowning the world’s best player every year. A specially commissioned china plate was also handed over by the town’s mayor before the 41-year-old Matthews, who was famously teetotal, gave a short speech. “He might have had a double carrot juice that day,” says his son, Stanley Matthews Jr, who will attend this year’s awards with his sister, Jean, and her two daughters. “There was no ceremony. ‘Here’s your Ballon d’Or, well done’, sort of thing. But obviously it’s grown over the years, and now it’s a huge event. We’re very excited.” Continue reading...

item.title: Ian Holloway’s circus: why the manager’s antics are no laughing matter for fans
item.description: Swindon manager has a history of viral outbursts but fans want a united club and manager they can support In Ian Holloway’s often madcap managerial orbit, this was simply the latest in a steady succession of eccentric outbursts. Eyes bulging as he spoke, he boomed the letter “D” and promptly stabbed himself in the chest with an imaginary dagger. Next came the letter “M” alongside a blow from another invisible knife. Finally, a “W” followed by a jab to the heart. “Dead. Man. Walking,” he declared, pausing for effect between words and briefly falling into an Oscar-worthy zombie stupor. “That’s how it feels.” To an offbeat press conference genre containing seagulls following trawlers and self-proclaimed special ones, it was a crazy new entry worthy of its subsequent viral nature. Holloway at his finest. Continue reading...

item.title: European football: Lazio beat Parma to top Serie A; Dortmund lead Bundesliga
item.description: Lazio win 2-1 while Roma draw 3-3 with Napoli Beier gives Dortmund win over Eintracht Frankfurt Lazio climbed to the top of Serie A with a 2-1 home win ⁠over Parma ⁠as Roma ​twice came from behind to secure a 3-3 draw with Napoli in a pulsating clash in Naples. Lazio have 22 points from their eight matches this ⁠season and are three points clear of champions Inter Milan, who have played a game fewer and host Fiorentina on Sunday. Lazio opened the scoring in the 50th minute as Kenneth Taylor ⁠struck his first of the season, before Parma’s Diego Carlos put the ball into his own net trying ​to cut out a cross. The visitors scored a ‌late consolation through Simone Lontani. Continue reading...

item.title: Glitch in Chelsea’s coding costs Alonso while resurgent Spurs are all systems go | Barney Ronay
item.description: Home side broke the game open with some unique corner routines, but a goalkeeping error ruined the plan There was an odd interlude at Stamford Bridge with 76 minutes gone and the score still 0-0, one of those moments where suddenly your brain seems to be on inside out, like trying to walk the wrong way down an escalator. Tottenham had a corner on the left-hand side, in a game that had felt to that point like an extended practice session, a refinement of systems, the football equivalent of watching two middle-aged men methodically emptying the dishwasher, adding salt, descaling the hoses, tutting over knives incorrectly slotted, cups in the wrong row. Continue reading...

item.title: Tottenham stun Chelsea for second league win in a week as Cole Palmer is sent off
item.description: There are days when Tottenham go into these big games and find ways to beat themselves. This time, though, they held their nerve at a ground where they have mostly only known doom. Spurs played with control, stayed patient and won at Stamford Bridge for the first time since 2018 after waiting for Chelsea to press the self-destruct button during a calamitous and comical ending to a cagey game. Chelsea were meant to have grown. Xabi Alonso had even praised his side’s emotional control and ability to manage awkward spells during the buildup, but perhaps that was asking for trouble. Chelsea, short of poise on and off the pitch, deserved to be beaten at home for the first time this season and there was plenty of blame to go around after Alonso got his tactics wrong, Mike Penders scored a ridiculous own goal and Cole Palmer was sent off after a lunge on Conor Gallagher when he was already on a booking. Continue reading...

item.title: Championship roundup: Southampton beat West Ham; QPR put five past Swansea
item.description: Hammers humbled at home; Swansea thrashed 5-0 Burnley sack manager Hayen after 4-1 loss at Lincoln Southampton announced themselves in the promotion race with a statement 3-2 win at the pre-season title favourites, West Ham . Kuryu Matsuki, James Bree and Lewis Dobbin were all on target in a chaotic first half, while Kyle Walker-Peters and Tomas Soucek replied for the Hammers. Nuno Espírito Santo’s side would have gone top with a win but instead saw their nine-match unbeaten run halted. There were thousands of empty seats by the end at the London Stadium, with those who stayed booing the Hammers off. Southampton, deducted four points at the start of the season, are now just two points behind West Ham. Continue reading...

The Belgian was appointed in the summer as the permanent successor to Scott Parker, who left in April with relegation from the Premier League inevitable. He leaves having won just one match, a 4-0 league victory at Watford on 10 October. Continue reading...

item.description: The wait goes on for David Moyes. The 63-year-old Scot must have been hoping that on his 14th visit to this stadium as Everton’s manager, his luck would change. Yet from the moment Ezri Konsa slammed home his first goal for Arsenal as the Premier League champions rediscovered their knack of scoring from set pieces, the writing was on the wall. While it took until midway through the second half for Gabriel Magalhães to make sure of the victory, Arsenal were never going to let slip the chance of moving level on points at the top with Manchester City after their defeat by Aston Villa earlier in the day. item.title: Maresca ‘not worried’ by Guéhi’s gaffes as Aston Villa end City’s flawless start
item.description: Defender costs three goals in past two league matches Emery praises ‘fantastic’ match-winner Jackson Enzo Maresca is not concerned by the form of Marc Guéhi despite the defender costing his side three goals in the past two Premier League matches, the Manchester City manager said after seeing his side lose in the league for the first time this season. Nicolas Jackson’s double earned Aston Villa a 2-1 victory at Villa Park after Guéhi was unable to control the ball for the opener. Instead he spilled it into the path of John McGinn, who played it to Jackson, allowing him to score the first of two goals. The defender was then substituted at half-time having been booked on 32 minutes. Guéhi’s errors allowed Ipswich to score twice against City last weekend. Continue reading...

item.title: Nicolas Jackson double sees Aston Villa end Manchester City’s perfect start
item.description: Manchester City added a loss in the Premier League to one to the Premier League, as their perfect record this season vanished without an independent commission in sight. Two of the most in-form strikers in England did battle and it was Nicolas Jackson’s double that meant his side came out on top against Erling Haaland. City are certainly fallible, losing for the fourth time in a row here, and it was a reminder that life will not always be as simple as their first seven games. Mistakes cost City as Marc Guéhi and Gianluigi Donnarumma were punished by Jackson, who will have taken great pleasure in ending the winning run of his former Chelsea manager Enzo Maresca. Continue reading...

item.title: Change captain? Play the kids? How to solve the problems at Manchester United
item.description: The beleaguered Michael Carrick’s job is on the line, but there are steps he can take to revive the stricken club The big question as Bournemouth arrive for Sunday’s 2pm kick-off at Old Trafford is whether Michael Carrick will show his authority by stripping the captaincy from Bruno Fernandes and/or dropping Manchester United’s five-times player of the year. On Friday, Carrick refused to deny he may do so, but the bigger picture concerns whether cashing in on the Portuguese and his fellow mutineer, Lisandro Martínez, in the winter window would be prescient to initiate a new era. Fernandes and Martínez are out of contract in the close season (the club has an extra year’s option in both cases) and, judging by recent behaviour, intend to leave. So yielding, say, £40m and £25m respectively for them in January would allow investment as the rebuild begins. Even a few days on, Fernandes’s words in Como seem incredible: “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” he said after Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation. Fernandes’s open questioning of the tactics is a challenge to the head coach’s authority and we wait to see how/if Carrick will face it down. If Carrick acts and proves he is not a lame duck then even if he is removed a favour is done for his successor. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Mourinho is ready for his clásico return – stock up on popcorn, folks!
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Football Daily has never had much time for conspiracy theories. Lee Harvey Oswald dunnit, Stanley Kubrick didn’t fake the moon landing, Vinícius Jr doesn’t have a body double and Miranda isn’t a secret traitor. But our Spidey senses picked up when the UK government announced their Be Ready campaign on Thursday night. In case you missed it, or live outside the UK and couldn’t care less about this weird little island, we’ve lifted this from our news story : “Every Briton is being urged to stock up to nine litres of bottled water and three days’ worth of food in new government guidance designed to ensure that households can survive a weather, cyber or other serious emergency. The Be Ready campaign is aimed at persuading people to stock up with supplies to last 72 hours, amid growing official concern about the impact of the climate crisis, technological dependency and hostile state threats.” Would it not be much easier all round if the two big clubs in Manchester simply swapped all playing and coaching staff before the next round of fixtures? United would finally get the squad that Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez clearly feel they deserve, one of serial winners who are worthy of the club’s fine history (and free of the whiners). Meanwhile, City would might get a team that would make them (somewhat) competitive in the lower tiers where they’re surely headed. And a manager who has coached there quite recently. Sure there’d be a few grumbles from the fans, but more importantly in the current football climate, think of all the potential new shirt sales, and the Us-Against-the-World mentality that Enzo Maresca would be able to instil in his team whose own supporters would even hate them. And no-one would even have to move house. It’s a win-win solution. Although, no, it’s United; so probably a win-high-scoring-draw-against-Wycombe solution” – Justin Kavanagh. Like all right-minded people, I only read Big Website to get my fill of news and information (ahem …). However, I did come across a recent piece in The New Yorker on James Daunt, the chief suit of the US book chain Barnes & Noble (no relation). The billionaire Russian oligarch, Alexander Mamut, asked him 20 years ago how much it would cost to buy Waterstones, and when he was told it would be £40m, he looked pleased and just said, ‘That’s less than Fernando Torres’, before adding, ‘It’s not even half a boat’. Odd reference points these billionaires” – Noble Francis. May I be the first of 1,057 Daniels to say thank you for the good luck message at the end of Thursday’s Football Daily. It has put a little extra pep in my step today” – Daniel Mee. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: Mamdani loves Arsenal. He should challenge them to cut ties with the UAE over Sudan | Sasha Lezhnev and John Prendergast
item.description: The New York mayor’s passion for the Gunners and human rights presents an opportunity to push back on the club’s lucrative UAE sponsorship Like him or not, there is no doubt that New York mayor Zohran Mamdani’s passion for certain issues is electric, and that passion played a large part in him getting elected. But today, two of his biggest passions are on a collision course. On one hand, Mamdani is now arguably the US’s most high-profile supporter of English Premier League champions Arsenal. A superfan since he was a child , he has put the Gunners into the American spotlight more than anyone since becoming mayor. The Empire State Building gleamed in Arsenal’s red and white when they won the Premier League title. He wrote an essay about what Arsenal’s championship means to him, talks about Arsenal at press conferences and interviews and inaugurated Thierry Henry Way near Times Square in honor of the Arsenal legend. Continue reading...

item.title: Pascal Gross: the obsessive runner keeping Brighton ‘one step ahead’ after fast start
item.description: Midfielder ‘who can never stand still’ has brought renewed energy to Seagulls since return to the club in January Most footballers like to spend their summers unwinding after a long season but not Pascal Gross. Having been part of the Germany squad eliminated in the quarter-finals of Euro 2024 , the midfielder entered – and won – a running race. Gross completed the 8.4km course on Juist, in the East Frisian islands, in 31 minutes and 35 seconds. He is not known as someone who courts attention, and his victory by more than a minute came to light only when a video was posted on social media by a competitor. Continue reading...

item.title: Chaotic state of football in Brazil epitomises a nation where greed has conquered glory | Jonathan Liew
item.description: The national game merely reflects the mood in a divided nation which is going to the polls with very little faith in the power of democracy Look, cards on the table: I don’t know for certain, and nor do you, whether Flávio Bolsonaro – the man widely tipped to become the next president of Brazil after Sunday night’s election – really did steal an island from Richarlison. There are lawyers involved, claims and counter-claims, and in any case, adjudicating land ownership disputes between right-wing strongmen and Tottenham reserve-team strikers lies very much beyond this column’s spectrum of expertise. It’s why, for example, this newspaper took no official position on the well-publicised battle between Rodrigo Duterte and Vincent Janssen over that Polynesian isthmus. According to Richarlison, a few years ago he purchased an island off the southern coast of Rio de Janeiro, and has the documentation to prove it. Richarlison says Bolsonaro tried to buy it from him, and when he refused a lawyer named Willer Tomaz simply turned up and annexed it. “These guys took the island without spending a penny, as far as I know,” Richarlison claimed in an Instagram video that has been viewed more than 31 million times. Tomaz has accused Richarlison of lying, arguing that he has a public deed registered at the notary’s office. Bolsonaro, for his part, has denied any connection with the island in question and described Richarlison’s intervention as “politically motivated”. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
item.description: Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends Premier League top scorers After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that marked the end for Ange Postecoglou , the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. Niall McVeigh Ipswich v Nottingham Forest, Friday 8pm BST Aston Villa v Manchester City, Saturday 12.30pm BST Arsenal v Everton, Saturday 3pm BST Coventry v Fulham, Saturday 3pm BST Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Post-Ferguson worn-out horror show continues at Manchester United
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! We’re in the midst of what the kids call “spooky season” – or, for our fellow fusty old-timers out there, “autumn”. If you’ve been cosying up with a few horror flicks this month, you’ll know nothing good can come from hanging around a lake at this time of year. And so it proved for Manchester United, who endured an early Halloween nightmare on the banks of Lake Como that may have driven a stake through the Michael Carrick era. Hailed as the interim anti-Amorim not so long ago, Carrick has overseen two wins this season, against Ipswich and Sabah Baku . Como were in Serie D when Carrick won Big Cup with United as a player in 2008 – now, 18 years on, he watched the Italian upstarts dance, twirl and shimmy through the set of training cones he had sent out to represent his storied club. Any chance the Independent Football Regulator could also force the sale of Manchester United while it is at it? – James Marriott. Belated birthday greetings to Florent Sinama-Pongolle, a player once described (by Big Website if memory serves) as the only footballer whose surname sounds like an art-house trend – Alan Burgess. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...
